items.quote: But as a percentage of sales price as I said, we are going to see gross profit margin expansion. And I think , as a percentage of sales price, construction cost to come down.

items.statement: Sales price improved 34% YoY to Rs 6,811 per sq ft in FY24
items.quote: Sales price improved to Rs. 6,811 for the year on a per square feet basis vis-à-vis Rs. 5,080 per square feet in the previous year, an increase of 34% on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: Plans to launch Amarah Phase-4, 5 and Sector 80 project in Gurugram in FY25
items.quote: We have Ashiana Amarah Phase-4 and 5 to launch. We are hoping to launch it in this financial year both those phases and we have another project in Sector 80 in Gurugram which is not too far away from Ashiana Amarah. Also, we are hoping that we can launch that in the 4th Quarter of this year and if not 4th Quarter of this year , then the first quarter of the next year.

items.statement: Has 80-90 lakh sq ft launch pipeline excluding Milakpur land
items.quote: So, we have about 80-90 lakhs square foot to launch excluding Milakpur between our future phases and l and banks.

items.statement: Senior living target of 900-1,000 units/year in 3-4 years from 354 currently
items.quote: Right now, we are looking at from a medium-term view if we can get to about 900 -1,000 units a year from about 354 units a year today as compared to last year.

items.statement: Will not pursue hybrid projects; committed to full senior living projects
items.quote: don't think hybrid projects are the way to go. We don't think they create the value that a senior living consumer wants. Again, these are different opinions and different people can have different strategies. We want to do a full senior living projects wherever we want to go

items.statement: Recorded highest ever pre-tax operating cash flows of Rs 304.46 crore in FY24
items.quote: During the year, we recorded pre-tax operating cash flows of Rs. 304.46 crores which was the highest ever.

items.statement: Buybacks expected every 3-5 years depending on cash flow availability
items.quote: Buybacks will not happen every year. We hope that we do buybacks every 3-5 years depending on the cash flow availability of the

items.statement: IFC holds >30% share of net cash flows in Amarah project initially, then 30%
items.quote: Their percentage share in the cash flows of the project would be a little bit more than 30% in the net cash flows of the project till a certain figure they have a higher share and then becomes 30 %.

items.statement: Targets 27-30% gross profit margin on JV projects at current prices
items.quote: So based on current sale prices and current cost of construction, we typically look for about 27% to 30% on JV projects.

items.statement: Conservative pre-sales guidance due to potential launch delays and project underperformance
items.quote: We might have a launch delay. We don't know what all things go wrong. In my experience in life, there has been only one law that is always applied and that's been Murphy's law. So , we are conservative in that front.

items.statement: Term sheets have ~50% failure rate during diligence
items.quote: But these things are 50% as sometimes term sheets slip somewhere or the other during diligence or something or the other.

items.statement: FY25 profit growth target of at least 20% over FY24's Rs 1,388 crore
items.quote: I think going forward next year, we at least see if all goes well and there are not too many surprises, we should do greater than 20% growth for the year.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth target of 15-20% and earnings growth of ~20%
items.quote: I think we believe that we shall be able to grow top line wise also more than 15% to 20% and even on earnings growth, also, we are looking at about 20% comfortably.

items.statement: Agrochemicals internal target to triple revenue to Rs 300 crore in 3 years
items.quote: our internal target is that this business has to triple in the next 3 years, we want to go to Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Annual capex of Rs 300-350 crore for maintenance and incremental capacity at existing sites
items.quote: we expect that we should spend about Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 350 crores a year is what we are spending in a year.

items.statement: Expanding capacity at existing sites; no new greenfield sites planned
items.quote: We are not building any new sites. But in the existing site itself, we are expanding capacity.

items.statement: RoW business performing well with Brazil at $25-26M, Canada at ~CAD 40M, and strong orders from Egypt and Saudi
items.quote: Brazil, I think direct exports and our subsidiary exports are almost $25 million to $26 million a year. Canadian sub has done nearly CAD 40 million. So, overall, our RoW business is doing well. I think this year , we have some very good orders from Egypt and Saudi.

items.statement: Margins sustainable if product mix holds; conservative 20% PAT growth guidance despite stable margins and 15-20% revenue growth
items.quote: Based on the product mix holding up, yes.

items.statement: Revlimid pricing trajectory driven by market dynamics; no specific guidance on future pricing
items.quote: It goes by the market dynamics. I think that's the answer I can give you.

items.statement: Key pipeline products: Semaglutide (FTF on certain strengths), Olaparib, Carfilzomib, Trabectedin, Imbruvica (subject to litigation), Kyprolis
items.quote: Semaglutide we mentioned, Olaparib we have mentioned. Carfilzomib, we have mentioned; Trabectedin, we have mentioned. So, I think this is all there in the investor presentation.

items.statement: Filed Rimegepant for migraine but faces 7-8 day-one filers; targeting 2-3 first-to-file approvals in next 2 years
items.quote: we filed a product called Rimegepant for migraine. But it was like, I think, 7 or 8 filers on day 1.

items.statement: Revlimid U.S. distribution agreement with Teva continues beyond Jan 2026 settlement on same terms
items.quote: Yes, we have an arrangement with Teva that will continue.

items.statement: Cannot draw parallels between Canada and U.S. Revlimid markets due to different dynamics, partners, and REMS requirements
items.quote: Canada is a completely different market. I mean, how the product is distributed and how the tender cycles work. So, to answer your question, no, you can't draw parallels, it's a different world.

items.statement: Kothur plant under regulatory scanner; derisking via two U.S.-approved sites (Hyderabad, Vizag) and CMO model for niche products
items.quote: we have 2 sites for the U.S. So, we have Hyd erabad, and we have Vizag. So, like Rimegepant that we filed recently, we filed from Vizag

items.statement: Actively seeking RoW/emerging market acquisition to strengthen base business; valuations more attractive than India
items.quote: we are looking at an acquisition and, in the RoW,. I think that's what we are looking at.

items.statement: Buyback under consideration if large acquisition not concluded; decision pending
items.quote: if we get a large enough acquisition then I don't want to do a buyback. But if we are unable to close a large acquisition, then maybe we can consider a buyback.

items.statement: Net cash position: Rs 2,004 crore cash/investments vs Rs 116 crore debt (Rs 40 cr EPC credit, Rs 76 cr self-liquidating bill discounting)
items.quote: Rs. 2,004 crores is cash and listed shares and investments and deposits and Rs. 116 crores is the debt we have as of today, yes.

items.statement: Domestic business model change caused one-time Rs 35 cr charge; run rate remains ~Rs 100 cr/quarter, growing 8-10%
items.quote: It's a onetime charge because we just changed a few things and the way we are distributing. I think the run rate is still 95% to 100%.

items.statement: Agrochemicals one-time Rs 30 cr hit for non-utilized intermediate capacity at third-party site due to price drop
items.quote: we had to make a provision for non -utilization of that. So, we took a hit on depreciation of amo unt and certain advance we gave to that supplier.

items.statement: ~5,000 employees excluding contractors; ~5,700-5,800 including contractors; employee cost ratio expected to sustain
items.quote: if we remove the contractors,is what about 5,000 employees in the system and if we include the contractors and everyone, I think it's about 5,700 to 5,800.

items.statement: Conservative guidance due to unforeseen risks; one-offs can occur from inventory, currency, or other moving parts
items.quote: There's always something that you never know will happen, right? So, why promise something. The other person asked me, is there going to be another one time. There's always something that will go wrong, right?

items.statement: gCopaxone (glatiramer) steady with two generics (Sandoz and Natco); slight volume decline due to shift to oral MS therapies
items.quote: It's been consistent. I think it's done well. there are only 2 generics, Sandoz and us. So, Mylan has done extremely well with this product.

items.statement: NCE in Phase II for oral cancer; early stage, no guidance provided
items.quote: So, we have 1 NCE, which is doing Phase II in the U.S. at this time and it's in the early days, so I think I will refrain from giving any guidances or any idea.

items.statement: Cellogen CAR-T investment is modest, early-stage; option to invest more based on progress
items.quote: It's a very early stage. I can't get into timelines and all, but I think we are excited, and I think we see that there are a lot of opportunities in this area.

items.statement: Red Sea/logistics impact minimal as niche products shipped by air; freight cost not significant portion of product value
items.quote: Our whole model is only doing niche and a lot of our shipments are by air , and compared to the value, the air freight component is not a significant portion of the costing.

items.statement: Domestic pharma business growing 8-10%; secondary sales consistent near Rs 100 cr/quarter
items.quote: We believe the business is growing around 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Agrochemicals FY24 revenue fell Rs 25-30 cr short of Rs 140-150 cr target due to bad monsoon and returns
items.quote: We wanted to do about Rs. 140 crores to Rs. 150 crores. I think those are our estimations, we fell short and by about Rs. 25 crores, Rs. 30 crores.

items.statement: Base business PAT (ex-Revlimid) estimated at Rs 350-400 crore
items.quote: It is probably around maybe Rs. 350 crores to Rs. 400 crores PAT, I would believe, yes.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR200-300 crore in FY26 and INR300-400 crore in FY27, totaling INR600-700 crore over next 3 years
items.quote: Swati so looking at the current fleet size we would definitely like to have a capex plan of about INR200 crores to INR300 crores next year w hich is 25 -26 and then 26 -27 around INR300 crores, INR400 crores. So put together about INR600 crores, INR700 crores capex will go in next 3 years

items.statement: Major part of capex to be funded through internal accruals
items.quote: And we believe that we are doing good profitability currently and we should only grow our profitability. So major part of this capex will be funded through the internal accruals.

items.statement: Market rates firm for next 2-3 years; East Coast opportunities growing over 5-7 years with new ONGC discoveries; targeting one 3-year contract opportunity
items.quote: to add over the next 4 to 5 years? Naveen Mohta: Yes on the East Coast a lso there's a lot of requirement is coming up with new discoveries and new oil production being flowing from ONGC from East Coast. So there's one exciting opportunity which we are targeting as of now and which we are looking to if that opportunity happens then we will be getting a 3 year kind of contract for that

items.statement: Maintaining healthy working capital cycle of 80-90 days; current debtors equivalent to Q3 billing
items.quote: So we are maintaining a healthy working capital cycle of around 90 days which we are maintaining throughout t he period. If you see the current debt this is equivalent to Q3 billing both are more or less equal. So we are maintaining the healthy cycle of 80 to 90 days

items.statement: Charter rates improved vs last year; trend expected to continue for 2-3 years; benefit depends on vessel availability for spot market
items.quote: So over -- compared to last year we have seen prices forming up which are giving us an advantage and I foresee t his trend to continue for next two-three years definitely. But again it all depends upon how many vessels are available to take that advantage for the spot market

items.statement: 3 vessels on long-term charter, 3 on 2-year spot contracts; non-monsoon vessels idle in Q2 and part of Q1
items.quote: Out of 6 vessels, 3 are already on a long -term charter. The balance 3 are also on a spot contract for 2 -year basis. So, there is no deviation or volatility in terms of the profitability. Only the 3 contracts that I mentioned on the later part are on non -monsoon season.

items.statement: Opening global office in London via UK subsidiary; acquired property for this purpose with INR180 crore loan
items.quote: This loan we have given to our UK subsidiary and we are in the process of opening our global office there in London. For that we have acquired some property. For its funding we have provided that term loan.

items.statement: Seasonality impacts Q1 (monsoon from mid-May) and Q2; 3 non-monsoon vessels idle during this period; year-on-year growth expected despite seasonality
items.quote: Even in Q1, since the monsoon hits around 15th of May onwards, so our three vessels which are on non -monsoon season only operate, they will not be operating after two months of Q1 and entire Q2. But however, we believe that on a year -on-year basis, we should be doing better.

items.statement: Future capex (replacement vs new addition) depends on DG shipping guidelines 2 years out
items.quote: So that depends Swati depending on 2 years down the line how DG shipping guidelines will come and how vessels are available. So i t can be either a replacement or new addition depending on the market opportunity

items.statement: Targets 25-30% loan book growth for FY25
items.quote: So about 25% to 30% is what we are approximately targeting.

items.statement: Expects average credit cost of 2.5-3% on steady state basis
items.quote: on an ongoing basis, on a steady state on average we expect about 2.5% to 3% of credit costs going forward.

items.statement: Targets 60-75 new branches plus split branches in FY25
items.quote: we are targeting anywhere from about 60 to 75 new branches plus certain split branches as well

items.statement: Expects borrowing cost to decline by at least 100 bps
items.quote: At least we are expecting 100 bps dip as is the market interest rates.

items.statement: NIMs expected to be largely protected despite lending rate cuts
items.quote: NIMs would be largely protected.

items.statement: Targets comfortable capital adequacy of 22-25% (4.5x debt-to-equity)
items.quote: Typically, we target about 4.5x of debt to equity. That comes out to 22%-25%or so.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM grew 36% YoY to INR 2,639 crores as of March 2024
items.quote: As on 31st March 2024, Arman' s consolidated assets under management stood at INR2,639 crores, registering a growth of 36% has compared to INR1,943 crores on 31st March 2023.

items.statement: Microfinance AUM grew 35% YoY to INR 2,193 crores; MSME AUM grew 44% YoY
items.quote: Our Microfinance and MSME AUM reported 35% and 44% year-on-year growth, respectively.

items.statement: Standalone AUM grew 42% YoY to INR 446 crores including Two-Wheeler and Micro LAP pilot
items.quote: Our stand-alone assets under management, which includes lending to micro enterprise Two-Wheeler loans, and of course, the new Micro LAP pilot vertical increased by 42% to INR446 crores as compared to INR315 crores on 31st March 2023.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 30% YoY to approximately INR 2,300 crores in FY24
items.quote: Despite the rigorous screening process, we reported a 30% growth in disbu rsements amounting to approximately INR 2300 crores, driven by robust and consistent demand during the review period that is FY '24.

items.statement: Rural Micro LAP pilot expects INR 6-7 crores disbursement in Q1 FY25
items.quote: This quarter we are predicting about a INR6 crores or INR7 crores disbursement.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated NIM at 15.2%; yield at 25.1%; cost-to-income at 26.6%
items.quote: Yield stood at 25.1%. Net interest margin stood at 15.2%. Cost to income stood at 26.6%.

items.statement: All-inclusive borrowing cost ~13% for FY24; down 50-75 bps in Q4 post QIP and rating upgrade
items.quote: So Amit, all costed out, it turns out to be about 13 %-odd for the year. But post the QIP, we've already seen the rates coming down by about 50 bps to 75 bps in the last quarter

items.statement: Lending rates being cut due to competition and regulatory pressure; yields declining
items.quote: We are cutting our lending rates, of course, for competition and of course, through different pressure that is announced by regulato rs and other things. So definitely the REITs have gone down

items.statement: GNPA 2.88%, NNPA 31 bps as of March 2024; consolidated collection efficiency 96.6% in March
items.quote: Our gross non performing assets, which is GNPA, stood at 2.88% and net non performing assets, which is NNPA, were at a low of 31 basis points for period ended 31st March 2024. Collection efficiency for the month of March in our Microfinance business stood at 96.5%. MSME business stood at 97.6%, and our Two -Wheeler business stood at 95.6%. Consolidated collection efficiency stood at 96.6%.

items.statement: Collection pressure due to heat, elections, and over-lending in certain areas; expects recovery in next couple of quarters
items.quote: Overall there is some pressure on the collections. Numerous factors at play. Of course, there is heat and there is elections, but largely speaking there's a lot of -- I mean in certain areas there has been a lot of over lending going on and that has been generating pressure for us on the repayment side. So hopefully it's nothing permanent and we can get it fixed in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Write-offs ~INR 40-45 crores (MFI ~40 cr, standalone ~5 cr); incremental provisions ~INR 20-25 crores in FY24
items.quote: So that impairment cost of INR65 crores, if you had to attribute it to increase in provisions versus write-offs, what Vivek is saying around INR40 crores to INR45 crores would be write-offs and INR20 crores to INR25 crores would be provision -- increase in provisions.

items.statement: Cumulative provisions at INR 90 crores (3.4% of AUM); management overlay included
items.quote: Cumulative provisions stood at INR90 crores, which is 3.4% of the consolidated assets under management. of these provisions for the Arman stand-alone business stood at INR17 crores, and for the subsidiary Namra stood at INR73 crores.

items.statement: Opened 67 new branches in FY24; total branch count 402; expanded into newer states
items.quote: In terms of branch expansion, we have opened 67 new branches over the last 12 months, bringing our total branch count to 402 branches. This expansion has been complemented by successful penetration into newer states and geographies where performance has been promising.

items.statement: Total borrowings INR 2,261 crores; debt-to-equity 1.8x; cash/liquidity INR 180 crores; CAR standalone 62.7%, Namra 32.8%
items.quote: Total borrowings amounted to INR2,261 crores, comprising of a diverse mix of financial instruments. We maintained substantial liquidity of about INR180 crores in c ash and bank balance, liquid investments and undrawn CC limits with a comfortable debt-to-equity ratio of 1.8 times, and a healthy capital adequacy ratio of 62.7% on a stand-alone basis.

items.statement: ~75% of customers have loans from other institutions; over-leveraging risk due to FOIR assessment challenges
items.quote: I think only about 20% to 25% of the customers are new to credit or... Vivek Modi: Unique to us. Alok Patel: Or unique to us overall. 75% of our customers would have another loan from some other institutions, whether it is a Kisan credit loan or a tractor l oan or an MFI loan or gold loan or what have you, right

items.statement: MFI ticket size increased from INR 28k to INR 46-47k over 3 years; moved from 12 to 24-month tenure to keep EMI affordable
items.quote: Specifically for us, we started -- when I started M icrofinance in 2010, it was INR10,000, 1 -year loan. And then the ticket sizes started going up, overall, the demand started going up more. Customers were not satisfied with just INR10,000. And so as the ticket size went up, the tenure went up. And so we switched to a 14-month product post which we switched to an 18-month product. And now we are

items.statement: Sector has 2-4 years before euphoric growth; 40% of India underpenetrated but difficult to access; current 25-30% growth not dangerous
items.quote: I don't think so. I mean overall, microfinance still has a good two to four years to go before it reaches that euphoric moment of growing faster than it needs to. Right now, I don't think that growing 25%, 30% is dangerous at all.

items.statement: ROA 7.6%, ROE 27.8% for FY24 (includes QIP proceeds); PAT grew 85% YoY to INR 174 crores
items.quote: Return on average AUM stood at 7.6%. Return on equity stood at 27.8%. And just as an FYI, this 27.8% ROE calculation includes the QIP proceeds of INR230 crores raised in the last week of December. So all in all, a great year.

items.statement: Operating expenses may be marginally higher in Q1 due to new branch hiring; settles by Q4
items.quote: Yes. So to answer your second quest ion first, yes, marginally operational expense, especially salaries initially might be higher. But by the end of the year, that catches up. So this is what typically happens during Q1, it's slightly higher. And by Q4, it settled down.

items.statement: Management targets minimum 15% YoY revenue growth over several years
items.quote: Our endeavor would be to grow as fast as possible. And we generally tend to focus on a 15-odd-percent Y-o-Y growth every year.

items.statement: Atraco normalized EBITDA margin expected at 10-10.5%, Matrix at ~11%, both to reach GE levels in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: In a normalized operations, Atraco should be over 10% to 10.5% EBITDA margin and Matrix should be at about 11% odd EBITDA margin on an ongoing basis.

items.statement: FY25 capex of INR100 crores allocated: INR40 cr for Bhopal unit, INR50 cr for efficiency/profitability improvements, INR10 cr for fabric processing unit
items.quote: For the Bhopal new unit, we allocated around INR 40 crores. For the normal capex, what Mr. Siva talked about, we will be investing in improving the efficiency parameters, that is the profitability improvement capex are the key focus area. We allocate d almost INR50 crores during the year for this purpose . INR25 crores for the existing units, about INR10 crores in Matrix and INR15 crores for Atrac

items.statement: Atraco and Matrix currently at 80-85% utilization; expected to reach near 100% by H2 FY25
items.quote: Utilization in both these entities, I would say, is around 80%, 85% at the moment of their capacity. I anticipate based on -- and this is a bit early for me to say, because orders for H2 will come only somewhere in Q2, so full visibility will come. But our expectation is that by second half of the year, both of them should go to at least close to 100% capacity utilization based on early indication

items.statement: Atraco has potential for 20-25% capacity expansion, revenue impact mainly in FY26
items.quote: I believe that you know for Atraco there is a possibility of 20 -25% capacity expansion possible and we will work towards it. Most of that revenue from that capacity expansion should play out in the subsequent year, FY26.

items.statement: Gokaldas standalone currently at 100% utilization, chock-a-block with orders
items.quote: Standalone entity, as we speak in the current state, we are at 100% in fact we are -- from a delivery standpoint, we have chock-a-block with orders. We are not able to take any more. So we are at 100%.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu fabric unit trial production ongoing, commercial production expected early Q2 FY25
items.quote: By this quarter, all the trials will be completed and commercial production should start early next quarter from the Tamil Nadu unit.

items.statement: Strong demand traction for existing entity; newly acquired entities need 2-3 quarters to ramp up demand
items.quote: We see strong demand traction for the existing entity while the newly acquired entities will require handholding for over 2 to 3 quarters to ramp up the demand from existing levels.

items.statement: Global apparel demand fell 20% in US, 19% in EU, 28% in UK in FY24 due to inventory overstock; destocking cycle ending
items.quote: For most part of FY '24, the retail industry continued to be in an inventory overstock position resulting in brands reducing their apparel purchases by 20% in the U.S., 19% in EU and 28% in U.K. The inventory destocking cycle is now coming to an end with many fashion brands showing reduced inventory, improved financial performance and the renewed appetite to buy.

items.statement: US sourcing growth expected ~10% in FY25 (not full 20% recovery) as brands remain cautious on interest rates
items.quote: But will the growth be 20%? The answer is no. It will be more like 10% or thereabouts as everybody is cautious till they see long -term traction in interest rates and, hence, demand outlook.

items.statement: Consolidated FY24 EBITDA margin 11.8%, pulled down by acquired entities; existing business delivered exceptional performance
items.quote: The company delivered an EBITDA margin of 11.8% for the year as the newly acquired entities pulled down the margin. The company continued to deliver exceptional performance in the existing business and is working towards continuous performance improvement of the acquired entities.

items.statement: Pricing power to return slowly over 3-4 quarters, full recovery more likely in FY26 than FY25
items.quote: As the situation improves going forward and the demand is coming back, the pricing power will come back. But my sense is the pricing power will take some more time before it reaches because the full demand situation has not been restored. Even in Q4, there was lower inputs compared to the Q4 of previous year. So it will change, it will slowly turn. But I suspect over the next 3 to 4 quarters, the

items.statement: Fabric is primary raw material; cotton price volatility has limited impact as fabric price is pass-through in contracts
items.quote: We buy fabric. Fabric is our raw material. And by the time, cotton prices get impact , cotton gets converted into fabric. Cottons component in fabric is low. And we tend to have fabric price as a pass -through when we tend to price our contract.

items.statement: Gokaldas standalone working capital cycle at 70 days (inventory 61, receivables 36, payables 24); target 70-75 days for FY25
items.quote: For the working capital cycle for Gokaldas, our inventory is at 61 days, receivables at 36 days and payables at 24 days. We are there with the 70 days target , while we tend to operate between 70 to 75 days, and we believe that is the same level we will continue in the current year also.

items.statement: Atraco working capital ~90 days (inventory 90, receivables 30, payables 30); Matrix ~75 days (inventory 50, receivables 50, payables 25)
items.quote: In Atraco, the inventory holding is 90 days and 30 days of receivables and payables is around 30 days. So , we operate with around 90 days working capital cycle in Atraco. Matrix, is again a similar model of our India operations, but at least there is a better efficiency in inventory management because they have back -to-back tie-up with the fabric processing house. So, they operate with a lower i

items.statement: Net debt INR336 cr as of Mar 31, 2024 after acquisitions; turned net cash positive after INR600 cr QIP in April 2024
items.quote: After the acquisition of these 2 companies through a combination of debt and equity, the company had a net debt of INR336 crores as of March 31, 2024. Subsequently, the company raised equity capital of INR600 crores through qualified institutional placement in April 2024, which has helped the company to turn net cash positive.

items.statement: Raised INR600 crores via QIP in April 2024, turning company net cash positive
items.quote: Subsequently, the company raised equity capital of INR600 crores through qualified institutional placement in April 2024, which has helped the company to turn net cash positive.

items.statement: Acquired Atraco (Jan 2024) and Matrix (late Mar 2024) for INR934 crores; integration on track, slightly ahead of plan
items.quote: are fully on. And there's a lot of work that is going on. Keep in mind that Atraco was acquired only in January and Matrix was acquired in the late, in almost end of March, so the end of that quarter. So it's only a few months since we have acquired now and integration efforts are fully on. We are seeing a lot of green shoots in that effort. So far, the integration is going very well as planned. A

items.statement: Only one customer overlap between Atraco and Gokaldas; no overlap between Atraco-Matrix or Matrix-Gokaldas; cross-selling discussions underway
items.quote: There is only one customer overlap in all seriousness. And that customer, we are doing very well on both sides between Atraco and Gokaldas. As far as Atraco and Gokaldas and Matrix or Atraco and Matrix are concerned, there are no customer overlap.

items.statement: FY24: shipped 29 million pieces; FY25 target at least 29 million pieces despite mix shift
items.quote: For FY '24, we shipped about 29 million pieces and my hope is in FY '25, even if the product mix changes to a little more outerwear, I believe we should still be able to do this or even better in terms of number of pieces shifted.

items.statement: Gokaldas standalone FY24 realization INR677/piece on 29M pieces; Matrix 19-day Q4: 215K pieces at INR540 realization
items.quote: Gokaldas is @ INR 677, with 29 million pcs for the full year , last year. As far as Atraco is concerned, we did 7.9 million pcs at INR 254. Matrix is very negligible because it's only for 19 days. We sold around 215,000 pcs and the realisation is about INR 540.

items.statement: PLI scheme and FTAs with key markets expected to drive growth
items.quote: Favorable currency, PLI and FTAs with key markets should drive the company forward towards a strong future.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 10%-15% for upcoming year
items.quote: At least 10%-15% volume growth should be there.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 margins impacted by lower realizations, higher costs, provisions and product mix
items.quote: While our Q4 revenues increased Y-o-Y and remained stable on a Q-o-Q basis, we experienced a notable impact on gross and EBITDA margins due to lower realizations and higher costs.

items.statement: CSR provision of Rs. 3-3.5 crore taken in Q4 FY24
items.quote: For example, the entire CSR was taken in the last quarter. It was around Rs. 3-3.5 crore of CSR was taken around that time.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margins at current levels; 15% achievable depending on product mix
items.quote: No, of course, it is sustainable. It all depends on the product mix. It depends on lots of things.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance INR 824 crores at end FY24; free cash flow INR 307 crores in FY24

items.statement: Merger with Cohance on track; received stock exchange approvals, awaiting SEBI approval before NCLT; timeline 12-15 months from Feb 2024
items.quote: We are progressing in line with what we had estimated. And I think we don't sense that the estimated timelines is going to overrun. But having said that, it is a regulated environment and we do need regulatory approval.

items.statement: M&A strategy focused on scouting meaningful technology platforms to accelerate Suven's growth
items.quote: Our pri mary intent is to ensure the Suven growth has to be accelerated. To do that, we have recognized some opport unities of technology platforms a s we are speak, we are constantly scouting for a meaningful technology platform s which will enable the Suven's growth

items.statement: Cohance CDMO business grew at 30% five-year CAGR and 20% YoY; Cohance revenue INR 1,341 crores with adjusted EBITDA margin 31.2%
items.quote: The CDMO business of Cohance has continued its growth streak with a full year CAGR of 30% and a year-on-year growth of CDMO at 20%.

items.statement: Cohance ADC platform growing significantly with commercial products, therapy expansion, market registrations; designer payloads in advanced development
items.quote: On the progress in the ADC segment, the ADC platform continues to grow significantly by its commercial products, therapy expansion and market registrations. Several other new products continue to be in developmental phase with innovator customers.

items.statement: Pashamylaram facility successfully completed FDA audit and other regulatory agency audits along with multiple customer audits
items.quote: Also glad to inform that we had a successful completion of FDA audit at our Pashamylaram facility and other regulatory agency audits along with multiple customer audits.

items.statement: Investing in high-quality manpower, expanding commercial engine, adding R&D scientists; Spec Chem getting senior BU head
items.quote: We are expanding and adding high- quality manpower, which is so very required for this business. I think we've already talked in the previous conversations also about a very strong commercial engine being made and that comes with a cost.

items.statement: ESG report to be released in coming quarter; Pashamylaram Unit 3 awarded EHS Excellence Award by CII and International Safety Award by British Safety Council
items.quote: We eagerly anticipate the release of Su ven's ESG report in the coming quarter, reaffirming our commitment to sustainable business practices. We are pleased to announce that our Pashamylaram Unit 3 site has been awarded the EHS Excellence Award by the CII.

items.statement: Medium-term CAGR growth forecast of 15%-20% maintained
items.quote: I have always been mentioning a 15%-20% kind of CAGR growth. And I think we have been slightly ahead of that. But I would expect that there should not be any change in the medium-term growth forecast.

items.statement: Glassware pressware furnace commissioned Jan 31, commercial production started Mar 28, 2024

items.statement: Opalware at 80% utilization, room to grow to 100%
items.quote: Coming to opal ware, we are at about 80% capacity utilization. And I think we have a good shot at going closer to the 100% level.

items.statement: FY25 capex budget ~INR 100 crores for de-bottlenecking, solar, furnace rebuilds
items.quote: About INR100 crores in capex this year. That is for some de-bottlenecking, some, another solar project, all put together will be about INR100 crores.

items.statement: ROCE expected to dip short-term then exceed 20% at 70-75% utilization
items.quote: But like I said, as far as calculations, once we are able to hit cross 70%, 75% capacity utilization, the ROCE of this business is north of 20%.

items.statement: Glassware growth expected substantially higher than 11% FY24 due to new capacity
items.quote: I do expect growth to be substantially higher than the 11% we had last year. The reason being as I mentioned, that we are able in the past also, we can add lots of new products and we have also some pricing advantages with our own manufacturing.

items.statement: Glassware and Opalware identified as main revenue growth drivers for FY25
items.quote: So the glassware and Opal ware, I would say would be the two main drivers of revenue growth this year.

items.statement: Inventory at ~2 quarters due to Opalware production at 100% vs 80% sales and BIS-related steel bottle imports

items.statement: Board approval for equity raise up to INR 250 crores, not yet executed
items.quote: I think we had already announced that we were looking for permission to raise equity up to INR 250 crores. We've not done anything yet on that but we have permission to raise equity up to INR 250 crores.

items.statement: Advertising spend at 7-8% of sales in FY24, similar planned for FY25
items.quote: It's going to be in the 7.5%. 7% to 8%.

items.statement: General trade largest channel, e-commerce second, weak in large format stores

items.statement: Team built for INR 2,000 cr scale; ESOPs and performance-linked compensation driving motivation

We also have, you know, ESOP schemes, which we give our people.

items.statement: Non-glassware: #1-2 on Amazon in OTGs, juicers; strong in bottles via personalization; trade channels still developing

items.statement: Scientific division backward integration capex on hold; not under consumer entity
items.quote: At the moment, so that will now come under scientific division. That will not come here. So that's mainly for scientific. But that's on hold only. I don't think we are at the moment looking to get into that.

items.quote: It's hard for me to give you specific numbers for FY '25. All I can say is that the Borosilicate furnace that we've added short-term may have some impact but I would say it would dramatically help improve EBITDA in, say, the coming year.

items.quote: this was close to around -- probably around 6% to 7% or so.

items.statement: Proprietary brand sales grew 46% to 10% of revenue, value-added diabetic/brown rice doubled

items.statement: Avoids high-risk markets Iran and Iraq despite volume opportunities, prioritizes profitability and cash flow security

items.quote: We plan to introduce MR LINAC Radiation Therapy in Bangalore, which would be a notable addition to the vastly superior radiation treatment offering at a HCGwhich will help us revolutionize radiation therapy in the state.

items.statement: Management aims to consistently deliver growth and performance, with multi-year contracts for next year higher than current revenue.
items.quote: The contracts in the next year are much higher than, the current numbers that we have done.

items.statement: Management does not see margins declining due to favorable exchange rates, productivity, reusable components, and larger multi-year contracts.
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, we do not believe that our margins will at all go down because everything is in favor the exchange rates are in favor, the productivity is in favor, reusable components and tools are in favor.

items.statement: Robust pipeline of signed businesses and multi-year contracts position the company for continued success.
items.quote: With a robust pipeline of signed businesses, we are well equipped to continue our trajectory of success in the upcoming year.

items.statement: Multi-year contracts signed for next year exceed current year revenue, providing revenue visibility.
items.quote: What we continuously and consistently try and achieve is that we have more signed contracts in hand for the next year before we end the current financial year.

items.statement: Capex is not a large portion of growth; investment focuses on talent, subsidiaries, market expansion, and potential acquisitions.
items.quote: Capex does not remain a very large portion of where the growth is done but investment does happen in creating subsidiaries, reaching out to new mark ets, reaching out to creating acquisitions or investments into scale-up startups

items.statement: Team grew from 250 to 400 engineers; targeting 40-60% year-on-year team growth, potentially doubling in 12 months.
items.quote: We do believe that on a year-on-year basis, we do add between 40%, to 60% of our team size. So, we are fairly geared at this point of time to grow from 400 to more than double in the next 12 months.

items.statement: Cybersecurity practice is a focus area with SOCs being set up in India and Netherlands for real-time monitoring.
items.quote: Shortly, we'll be setting up a Securities Oper ations Center, a SOC, in both India and the Netherlands. This is where a fa ir amount of investment will also

items.statement: 95% revenue from overseas (Nordics, Benelux, Germany, UK), 5% domestic; no single customer >20% of revenue.
items.quote: Almost 95% of our revenue comes from overseas customers and around 4%-5% comes from domestic customers.

items.statement: Shift to local entity in Netherlands enables higher billing rates and larger multi-year deals.
items.quote: This strategic shift from an outsourcing Company to a local entity in a local market, delivering local relationships and local culture, has significantly boosted our revenue and growth and enabled us to close larger multi-year deals.

items.statement: Active treasury desk hedges FX flows for at least 3 years.
items.quote: We at least make sure that we are fairly covered for at least 3 years. And we have a very active treasury desk towards making sure that we maintain our FX flows.

items.statement: Key risks include geopolitical instability, customer acquisition, technology changes; mitigated by diversification, FX hedging, and customer concentration limits.
items.quote: Somewhere war happens or somewhere political instability happens or the law changes in certain countries or your customers' businesses get acquired overnight and you lose control on your relationship.

items.statement: R&D spend estimated at 4-4.5% of revenue (INR4-5 crores in FY24), expensed not capitalized.
items.quote: Around INR4 crores to INR5 crores, yes.

items.statement: Priority is reinvestment for growth; dividend decision rests with board, but management recommends staying highly invested in growth.
items.quote: I would recommend to my board of directors to remain highly invested into growth and make sure that our shareholders remain as our top priority and we give them maximum growth along with the organization's growth.

items.statement: Competes with firms like Sogeti, TEOTO in Nordics/Benelux; differentiation via consulting depth, onsite presence, non-English market expertise.
items.quote: We compete with, let's say, Sogeti from France or we compete with TEOTO and every kind of players in the Nordics or we compete with a few names in the Benelux ecosystem.

items.statement: Stable Indian government supports global respect for Indian tech companies.
items.quote: Hopefully, if our results happen the way they are of our country, we get stable government. That means a lot to us on a global scale because Indian tech Company is hugely respected and appreciated on a global scale.

items.statement: Potential acquisitions or investments in scale-up startups are part of immediate strategies.
items.quote: investment does happen in creating subsidiaries, reaching out to new mark ets, reaching out to creating acquisitions or investments into scale-up startups and so on and so forth which do remain as some of the immediate strategies

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 11.7%, up 140 bps YoY; FY24 EBITDA margin 11.5%, up 50 bps YoY
items.quote: Operating EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 11.7%, up by 140 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve with softening raw material prices
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect our margins to improve with the softening of key raw material prices.

items.statement: FY25 margin to remain more or less same as no price hikes planned; focus on volume growth
items.quote: Margin will be more or less same because we're not taking any price hikes. We want to increase the volume.

items.statement: Target retail revenue ₹650-700 cr in 3 years with EBITDA margin 17-18%
items.quote: We have an annual growth plan of around 12%-15% in the retail segment. And we are having an EBITDA margin of around 16% to 17%. So with the growth coming back in the retail, we expect to be around ₹650 crores to ₹700 crores in retail and EBITDA margin of around 17% to 18%.

items.statement: Plan to open 25 COCO and 70 franchisee stores in FY25, expecting 6-7% value growth from expansion
items.quote: We will be opening around 25 COCO and around 70 Franchisees. So, we expect in our value terms, around 6% to 7% growth from this expansion.

items.quote: Our distribution network includes 753 distributors with an addition of 81 distributors this year. The east zone remains particularly strong with 482 distributors.

items.quote: In regard to demand in retail, it is muted, still , t here are 2-3 reasons for that. items.quote: What we are thinking maybe in this -- I mean, the lower segment, we may a little bit cut down the prices and bring back the volume so that the overall sales of the company increases.

items.statement: Retail contribution 61% in Q4, 65% in FY24; distribution 35% in Q4, 31% in FY24
items.quote: Retail sales contributed 61% in Q4FY24 and 65% for the full fiscal year.

items.quote: The sub-brands last year was around 57% and this year, it is around 59%.

items.quote: BIS inventory, there has been time given to liquidate the stock also. So, most of the stocks have been sold. Some stocks are there. That is also we are trying to sell it out and discounts are given in the EOSS season.

items.quote: We'll definitely try to reduce the inventory days and the debtors days. But it will be because the ratio remains the same. So, working capital also remains the same.

items.statement: Management aims for healthy growth in EBITDA and PAT in FY25 versus FY24, but declines to give specific top-line growth numbers.
items.quote: I would not like to speculate in specific numbers. It's early on, but I can say with confidence that we are a bottom line-driven company as I always have been saying in my previous interactions. And my EBITDA and profit, you should see a healthy growth vis-a-vis '23-'24.

items.statement: Management targets defending consolidated EBITDA margins near 27% and PAT margins near 20% achieved in Q4 FY24, though acknowledges it will be tough.
items.quote: In terms of Margins, yes, we will try to defend them or protect them to as close to these levels as possible.

items.statement: Order book stood at INR 5,700 crore as of 31 March 2024, comprising INR 2,600 crore consultancy, INR 2,500 crore turnkey, INR 300 crore export (Mozambique), and INR 300 crore leasing and subsidiary.
items.quote: The order book as of 31st March is INR5,700 crore. Consultancy is INR2,600 crore. Turnkey is INR2,500 crore. Export is the order of Mozambique, which is about INR300 crore, and the balance leasing and subsidiary, et cetera, is INR300 crore.

items.statement: Bangladesh export order of INR 915 crore for 200 coaches signed in April 2024, not included in March order book; revenue expected to start by Q3-Q4 FY25.
items.quote: The INR915 crore order of Bangladesh came in April. So we have not added that to the order book. But now that's also a finite order and a contract agreement has also been signed.

items.statement: Capex will remain in the range of INR 100-140 crore annually, consistent with low capex business model.
items.quote: Two, we are a low capex company. Our capex will always be in the range of INR100-odd crore, INR130 crore to INR140 crore, as you see from the trend.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio was 95.2% for FY24; management commits to continue returning best to shareholders as EBITDA and PAT grow.
items.quote: Our dividend payout ratio has been 95.2% for FY24. And as we grow and as we aim to grow in both our EBITDA PAT, we will continue to give our best to our shareholders.

items.statement: Order inflow momentum improved to one order per day in Q3 and Q4 FY24, with 100+ orders worth INR 940 crore in Q4; management targets maintaining this rate in FY25.
items.quote: We got 100-plus orders totaling to INR940 crore. And the way the trend is, these orders both export and consultancy orders, which we have been getting across sectors, I think we are confident that the FY24, which is a year of consolidation.

items.statement: Two export orders won after 4-year gap: INR 300 crore for 10 locomotives from Mozambique and INR 915 crore for 200 coaches from Bangladesh; both global tenders with tighter margins.
items.quote: These 2 orders in the last few months, INR300 crore plus and INR900 crore is a good step after a gap of 4-plus years. This INR900 crore from Bangladesh is for 200 coaches and INR300 crore from Mozambique, is for 10 locomotives.

items.statement: Export margins on new global tender orders will be much tighter than historical 20-25% range; management aims to optimize execution to improve margins.
items.quote: But fact that getting these orders on global tenders, the margins will be much, much tighter than the erstwhile export margins, which were in the range of 20%, 25%.

items.statement: Quality Assurance business client mix flipped from 2/3 Indian Railways to over 50% non-IR clients by end of FY24, with orders from defence, power, urban infra, PM Vishwakarma (INR 67 crore) and GeM portal (INR 14-15 crore).
items.quote: By the end of Q4, it has changed over that more than 50% to 55% is non-IR clients. We have got some interesting orders across spectrum, whether it is defence, whether it is power distribution, discoms, whether it is the sewage or urban infra or water or PM Vishwakarma quality checks order of INR 67 crore for the tool kits being supplied.

items.statement: Consultancy revenue (consolidated) reached all-time high of INR 1,300 crore in FY24, up 10% year-on-year in project consultancy.
items.quote: In fact, the total consultancy revenue (consolidated) reached a figure of about INR1,300 crore, which is an all-time high, which was a huge satisfaction to us because it is moving in the right trend and could help minimize the impact of the 2 challenges.

items.statement: Bangladesh coach order (200 coaches, 8 types) to start prototype production in a month; revenue realization targeted by Q3-Q4 FY25. Locomotive order (10 units) longer cycle, revenue may slip to early FY26.
items.quote: We recently on 20th May signed the formal contract agreement also. So now the final designs and approvals are underway and we will start production of the prototype and manufacturing very soon in a month or so.

items.statement: Turnkey order book of INR 2,500 crore executable over roughly 2.5-3 years; fresh turnkey orders limited to ~INR 500 crore in FY24.
items.quote: See, Tunrkey, by nature on average take about 2.5 to 3 years on an average. Some may take more. We are taking a limited turnkey projects. In fact, if you see the fresh orders in our turnkey have been only in the range of about INR500-odd crore in the last FY.

items.statement: Turnkey margins range 3-4%; consultancy margins ~45% in Q4 but under pressure from competitive bidding in both project consultancy and QA.
items.quote: Turnkey business by nature have a margin ranging from 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Management claims RITES is the only Indian company with full-spectrum infrastructure consultancy across 13 verticals (airports, ports, highways, metros, rail, buildings, etc.) under one roof.
items.quote: Interestingly, we can say with confidence that in the infrastructure consultancy business, we are maybe the only Indian company, whether in the PSU space or private space, which has all areas of infrastructure consultancy, except maybe oil and natural gas under one roof.

items.statement: Leasing business seeing growing client base across private and public sectors (power, cement, ports, steel); competition increasing but management targets higher revenue and EBITDA.
items.quote: Number of new clients, both in the private and public sector have been approaching us. And we are moving in the right direction in expanding our client base in the leasing business.

items.statement: REMC (subsidiary) signed first PPA for 900 MW round-the-clock tender, second LOA for 700 MW issued; solar plant at Bhilai inaugurated; revenue up 30%+, PAT up 37%+, dividend ~INR 80 crore (51% to RITES).
items.quote: The first PPA of 900 megawatts was signed. The second LOA for 700 megawatts RTC tenders is issued. There have been initiatives under the solar power plant Bhilai getting inaugurated under the developer mode.

items.statement: Shift from nomination to competitive bidding across consultancy and export orders compressing margins; management focuses on cost optimization and faster execution to protect profitability.
items.quote: The change, which happened about 2.5 years back in terms of nomination vis-a-vis competitive mode. That is the major change, which has been there for about 2, 2.5 years.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free; business model emphasizes low capex, no construction risk, and bottom-line focus.
items.quote: One, we are a debt-free company. Two, we are a low capex company. Our capex will always be in the range of INR100-odd crore, INR130 crore to INR140 crore, as you see from the trend. Three, we are not going to be a construction company.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs 2,000 crore, approximately 2x FY24
items.quote: In FY '25, on a consolidated basis, Gensol is projected to achieve the milestone of Rs. 2,000 crore revenue, approximately 2x growth from what we did in FY '24.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 25-26%
items.quote: We see that we should continue to do the similar kind of numbers.

items.statement: Solar order book at Rs 1,448 crore as of FY24 end with large pipeline
items.quote: Our solar order book stands at Rs. 1,448 crores as on FY '24 end with a big pipeline that far surpasses the number.

items.quote: approximately out of the Rs. 1,700 crore order books, Scorpius would have about a Rs. 100 crore-ish order book.

items.quote: The Indian market, the bid pipeline that we have today is about close to Rs. 3,000 crores of bid pipeline that we have.

items.quote: Currently, we are undertaking further validation and testing, including extreme weather conditions and vibration testing and some supply chain optimization, which is expected to complete by Q2 FY '25, when we will also start the test production for our customers and on-road testing.

items.statement: India targeting 300+ GW solar by FY30; long runway for solar EPC and BESS orders
items.quote: I think we are seeing that India is going to have some 300 plus gigawatt of solar power by FY '30, which means that there is going to be no dearth of orders for solar, no dearth of orders for battery energy storage systems.

items.statement: Scorpius Trackers revenue expected to double FY24 to FY25; US market entry from FY26
items.quote: The Scorpius Tracker, the revenue from there is expected to actually double between FY '24 and FY '25.

items.quote: we are expecting that we will have a revenue of between Rs. 50 and Rs. 100 crores from EV manufacturing in FY '25.

items.quote: So, it's greater than 50%, sir.

items.quote: We have recently appointed Ms. Shilpa Urhekar as the CEO of our EPC business. She was previously the national head at Sterling Wilson.

items.quote: As of late Feb '24, we have received ARAI certification for the vehicle, an important milestone validating the vehicle's performance, safety and compliance to vehicle regulatory norms.
