items.statement: Coex selling prices directly linked to raw material price; polymer prices down ~11% led to price adjustments
items.quote: whether we take, in the Coex business, we are selling prices directly linked to the raw material price. And that, is two-thirds of our business. So, when the raw material price went down 11%, straightaway that would hav e had a direct impact and the price would have gone down.

items.statement: New lines will start at modal range (6-8 micron) then move downwards; capability to produce below 2 micron
items.quote: when we start our new lines, of course, we will start at the mod al range and then move downwards. So, the lines will deliver market requirement.

items.statement: Globally only a handful of established dielectric film companies outside China; Chinese competition at lower end
items.quote: there are only a handful of good companies in this business. Other than China, which has a proliferation of companies, globally, you can probably count on one hand the established companies in this business.

items.statement: India-UAE CEPA free trade agreement and India-Middle East corridor benefits factored into UAE location decision
items.quote: India and the Middl e East, India and the UAE have in place an FTA agreement called the CEPA, which allows free trade across. Notwithstanding that, I'm going to be in a free zone in the UAE.

items.statement: Repaid INR15.31 crores working capital term loans under government guaranteed schemes well before schedule; no outstanding term borrowings for existing operations
items.quote: Continuing to reduce term loans for existing operations, during the year we repaid INR15.31 crores of outstanding working capital term loans under the guaranteed emergency credit line government guaranteed schemes which were actually repaid well before schedu le. There are now no outstanding term borrowings for existing operations

items.statement: Key expansion lines 85% funded by supplier credit in nature of ECB (Hermes backed insurance backed)
items.quote: the key lines are 85% funded by, 85% of their costs are actually funded by supplier credit in the nature of an ECB. Right. So, which is things like Hermes backed, which are insurance backed.

items.statement: Raised ~INR290 crores via warrants (INR140 crores) and QIP (INR150 crores) to support strategic vision and timing before political uncertainties
items.quote: Total capital raised during the year was approximately INR290 crores.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR2 per equity share on expanded capital
items.quote: The board has recommended a dividend of INR2 per equity share on the expanded capital of the company.

items.statement: Solar power installation ~90% complete at Ranjangaon; lower cost solar energy via open access expected before December
items.quote: The installation of generation equipment of solar power generation equipment is approximately 90% complete. Tata Power had communicated some delays in transmission system. However we anticipate that the supply of lower cost solar energy through open access to the company's Ranjangaon unit would commence well before December this year.

items.statement: Dielectric film sales volumes ~3,600 tons in FY24 similar to prior year
items.quote: The Biax dispatches or the Biax sales were like in the earlier year, very similar. It was 3,600 and something tons.

items.statement: European supply chain issues may delay some equipment arrival but no significant delay evident in broad timeline
items.quote: While the possibility that European supply chain issues may delay the arrival of some equipment, and this fact cannot be fully ruled out but at the present moment any significant delay in the broad timeline announced is not evident.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20% to 25% for FY25 on a conservative basis
items.quote: In terms of our projections, we anticipate a substantial revenue growth of 20 % to 25% in the fiscal year '24 to '25.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 43% to 48% for FY25
items.quote: And margins will be around 43 % to 48% as discussed in the previous con calls also for the upcoming financial year?

items.statement: Acquired 80% stake in Tippett Studio for $3 million USD
items.quote: That is -- we have purchased 80 percentage of stake for an amount of $3 million.

items.statement: Tippett Studio acquisition expected to complete in 30-45 days
items.quote: So, the acquisition is still in process. This is yet to be completed. So, probably in another 30 to 45 days, we are expecting all the legalities to be done and the completion to take place.

items.statement: Signed $5-6 million worth of projects globally for H1 FY25
items.quote: We already have signed up to 5 to 6 million projects globally.

items.statement: Project flow expected to surge from July onwards after strikes ended
items.quote: And the scope for new projects is so high and we are expecting a very huge surge in project flow from July onwards.

items.statement: H2 FY24 EBITDA margin at 47.08%, up 876 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA soared by 87.29, Y-o-Y to INR23.16 crores, translating to an EBITDA margin of 47.08%. An increase of 876 BPS from H2 FY '23.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain FY24 margins, potentially higher if projects materialize
items.quote: So the margin, we'll try to maintain wha t was declared in March '24. But if everything comes through, we'll try for a actually much higher than that

items.statement: Incurred INR13 crores of INR16 crores planned capex in FY24
items.quote: We have spent almost out of INR16 crores capital expenditure, we did INR13 crores.

items.statement: H2 FY24 revenue split: 60% domestic, 40% international
items.quote: The second half, I would say that 40% comes from the international and 60% from the domestic.

items.statement: Targeting 60% international, 40% domestic revenue mix in FY25
items.quote: So, this current year we are planning exactly reverse. 60% from OCs and 40% in domestic.

items.statement: Plan to add 250-300 employees across India, US, Canada in FY25
items.quote: this growth trajectory will enable us to expand our workforce by 250 to 300 employees across key regions such as India, the US, and Canada

items.statement: Expanding into animation and gaming segments to broaden service offerings
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are planning to expand into animation and gaming segments to broaden our service offerings and tap into new markets.

items.statement: Partially acquiring gaming companies to add technical coding capabilities
items.quote: The current year, we are looking at a couple of companies where we will partially acquire takes from them. And we are already working with a lot of gaming companies, developing assets and creatives.

items.statement: AI implementation reduced concept sketch time from 15-20 days to 2-3 days
items.quote: For example, when we develop concept sketches, we used to take 15 -20 days before. Now, we are doing it in 2-3 days.

items.statement: AI tools cut certain job time from 20 days to 3-4 days, boosting productivity
items.quote: Certain jobs that we do, we were spending a lot of time, at least 20 days of time, before AI intervention. And now we are simply doing it in 3-4 days.

items.statement: H2 FY24 total income grew 52.46% YoY to INR49.20 crores
items.quote: Our total income surged by an impressive 52.46% year -on-year, reaching INR49.20 crores up from INR32.27 crores in H2 FY '23.

items.statement: FY24 total income grew 53.96% YoY to INR90.43 crores
items.quote: For FY '24, the company maintained its momentum, with total income growing by 53.96%, Y-o-Y to 90.43.

items.statement: FY24 net profit grew 48.89% YoY to INR24.11 crores
items.quote: The net profit was INR24.11 crores, up by 48.89% year-on-year.

items.statement: No plans for further equity dilution or debt raise in FY25, internal accruals sufficient
items.quote: Sir, as such, we do not have any idea to dilute further either from the company side or from the promoter side because the money whatever we have secured as of now has been kind of enough to meet out the expansion program.

items.statement: Global marketing offices in US, Canada, Dubai, UK to expand client reach
items.quote: Additionally, we are expanding our presence in key markets with global marketing offices in the US, Canada, Dubai and UK, to cater to a broader client base.

items.statement: Receivables risk managed by withholding final delivery until milestone payments received
items.quote: What hold we have is, we don't deliver the final output. We might be working on, there are the most of the numbers that you see are from the work in progress of the project. So, what happens is, towards the delivery, we will be recouping and in certain milestones, we will be recouping.

items.statement: Ayalaan movie receivables of INR9-10 crores expected in 30-40 days from China and satellite rights
items.quote: For the Ayalaan movie, we have almost acquired most of the money and few areas we hold the rights for the movie, especially in China and few satellites. Most probably, I would say we are expecting th e inflow most probably in 30 -40 days maximum it will require

items.statement: Capex plan of Rs 1,000 crores over next 3 years, ~Rs 300 crores per annum
items.quote: We have also lined up the capital program for about Rs.1,000 crores in the next 3 years to drill a substantial number of developments and exploratory wells.

items.statement: Eastern region capex of Rs 250 crores over next two financial years
items.quote: In eastern region, the expected capital outlay for the next two financial years is about Rs. 250 crores, which will be further added if there is sustained demand for gas supply.

items.statement: B-80 field to resume normal production after flowline cleanup; targeting pre-cyclone levels
items.quote: We honestly hope that this will help us to test the optimum potential of the well D1 and D2 and get a sustained flow rate. This period of shutdown should be minimal and we believe that the field will come up to normal production level by producing from both the wells.

items.statement: Dirok field can produce 45-50 MMSCFD but curtailed due to lack of demand
items.value: 45 to 50 million cubic feet per day
items.quote: If the wells are intact, we can be able to supply 45 to 50 million cubic feet per day even tomorrow morning. But the fact remains, we don't have the demand for that uptake. That's the reason we have to curtail ourselves.

items.statement: Dirok gas sales limited by demand; nominated blocks of OIL/ONGC sell at lower ceiling price of $6.5/MMBTU vs HOEC's PPAC price of $8.82/MMBTU
items.quote: Major players, OIL and ONGC are selling the gas at the price applicable for nominated blocks. We are selling the gas at the PPAC price without any discount. Therefore, the gas from the nominated field is sold first and the balance demand is met by us at PPAC price.

items.statement: Standalone loan Rs 75 crores, subsidiary loan Rs 58 crores as of May 31, 2024; repaid Rs 242 crores in FY24; 'A' stable rating for Rs 500 crores
items.quote: As on 31 st May 2024, the outstanding loan in the standalone account is Rs. 75 crores and in the subsidiary account is about Rs. 58 crores. The company has repaid the loan of Rs. 242 crores in the current financial year. The company has “A” stable rating for Rs. 500 crores, bank loan from India rating.

items.statement: Environmental clearance for Cambay blocks delayed; submitted clarifications to EAC, expect clearance by June 2024
items.quote: EC was expected before March. However, it is delayed. We have submitted the due clarification for all queries raised by the EAC and we expect the clearance by June ’24.

items.statement: Applied for 2-year RSC extension for AA-ONHP-2017/19 block; drilling to commence after MOPNG registration
items.quote: Due to heavy rain, drill fire and approach road could not be constructed in time to move the rig for drilling before August 2024. We have made an application for two years RSC extension. And once the extension is registered from MOPNG, we will drill one exploration well.

items.statement: B-80 current production mix ~1,400 barrels oil/day and almost equal gas volume
items.quote: And mixed as such, we are producing about, say, 1,400 barrels of oil and gas is almost equal in B-80 now.

items.statement: B-80 facility uptime improved from 60% in FY23 to 86% in FY24
items.quote: As you see that uptime of the facilities of '22-'23 was about 60%, that we have increased to 86% in '23-'24.

items.statement: B-80 flowline wax blockage requires continuous chemical injection and periodic steam cleaning; uninsulated risers cause temperature drop
items.quote: In essence, there is an element of heat is required in the oil getting pumped into the export flow line. If the temperature is high, then there would not be any wax formation. If the temperature is low, that continues to have a wax formation. This is the process, and we are learning, and we know how to clean up in once in three months.

items.statement: Monsoon unpredictability poses risk to B-80 operations despite SBM maintenance and hose replacement
items.quote: We have carried out all the precautionary measures and the inspection and change of hoses and the maintenance of the SBM is carried out and under buoy hose inspection also carried out. And now no one can predict the fury of the monsoon. That's the position.

items.statement: FSO stock value Rs 33 crores as of March 31, 2024 vs Rs 73 crores previous year
items.quote: Value in stock in FSO as on 31 st March is Rs. 33 crores whereas the value in stock in FSO in the previous year was Rs. 73 crores.

items.statement: No production guidance given for FY25; dependent on B-80 stability and Dirok demand pickup
items.quote: So we, because I don't go for any projections for this business, basically, because many important things we have to come up with. We can have the reference projections. We would be improving our current production level once both the wells are flowing from the B-80. And if there is an increase in the demand from the Dirok field.

items.statement: Management expects more stable growth in next financial year with Dirok production, B-80 stability, Kharsang drilling and Western region workovers
items.quote: But we believe that the next financial year, once the Dirok production comes and the stability on B-80 production and drilling of Kharsang and some of the workovers which we are doing it in Dirok and the wells to be drilled in Western region, this will all give some more stability in a growth mode, with growth.

items.statement: B-80 Q1 FY25 operational days ~25 days due to flowline blockage
items.quote: About 25 days. 25 days on

items.statement: First well at PY-1 planned for June 2025 after expert review of drilling locations
items.quote: Once it is through, the first well we are planning in June 2025. That's what our plan at the moment.

items.statement: PY-1 subsea facilities can evacuate up to 55 mmscfd gas and 2,000 bpd condensate
items.value: 55 million cubic feet of gas and about 2,000 barrel of condensate
items.quote: All we can evacuate up to 55 million cubic feet of gas and about 2,000 barrel of condensate.

items.statement: B-80 facility uptime improved from 60% in FY23 to over 88% in FY24, targeting 90-95%
items.quote: You look at the uptime of the facilities of '22-'23. It was about 60%. Now it has gone more than 88%. So, in a manner that we will gradually improve, it comes around 90% to 95%.

items.statement: B-80 gas price reset to 12.2% of Brent via e-auction, down from ~22% previously
items.quote: I think, we have extended, we have got the e-auction completed and the price we will be now getting is about 12.2% of the Brent price, which was much higher in the previous year. It is about 22%, now reduced to 12%.

items.statement: B-80 gas realization expected to fall to $10-11/mmbtu from ~$16 average last year
items.quote: That will stand reduced to now $10 to $11.

items.statement: All future capex to be funded from internal accruals; no borrowings planned
items.quote: We plan for it. No borrowings anymore. They will be all capital expenditure through internal accruals.

items.statement: Dirok FY24 net revenue Rs 161 cr vs Rs 250 cr in FY23; B-80 FY24 revenue Rs 259-260 cr vs Rs 175 cr in FY23
items.quote: Dirok, it was the revenue, net revenue is about Rs. 250 crores, got reduced to Rs. 161 crores. And then what else you wanted to know? Dirok, Kharsang. Kharsang is a very minimal contribution. It is not much. So, we are ramping up the production by drilling the new well. And the B-80, when you look at the whole thing as such, it is about Rs. 175 crores in the last year. That has gone up to Rs. 259

items.statement: FY24 margins fell due to Rs 75 cr revenue loss at Dirok (demand) partly offset by Rs 55-60 cr gain at B-80
items.quote: See, we were in the similar line of '22-'23 comparing to '23-'24 because what has happened was there was about some Rs. 80 crores reduction on account of, some Rs. 75 crores virtually, that is the reduction in the Dirok and about Rs. 55 to 60 crore increase in the B-80.

items.statement: Management expects margins to improve if Dirok reaches 35-40 mmscfd and B-80 sustains 90%+ uptime
items.quote: I think we will be doing better. That's what we believe in. But it depends on many encounters which are not in our control.

items.statement: B-80 MOPU/FSO operating cost ~$140,000 per day; charged only on production days
items.quote: So, it's about $140,000 per day. Now that you divide it by 2,500 barrels of oil equivalent, that would be the variable cost, right. That is more or less fixed actually.

items.statement: B-80 line flushing shutdown expected in 2-10 days; equipment on site, work imminent
items.quote: The equipment is already on board. They will be starting the work once they line up, it may be taking a couple of days. And that's a period we will go for a small period of shutdown.

items.statement: PY-1 PSC extension of 10 years expected; production likely FY27-28
items.quote: We believe that will get extended by additional 10 more years. Normally, any producing field, they don't shut down. They will give extension. That's what we believe in it.

items.statement: Reserve life estimated at minimum 15-20 years; targeting reserve replacement via PY-1, Dirok, B-80, Kharsang, Block 19, Asjol, North Balol
items.quote: So, we are expecting this field and the potential and are looking at a minimum period of at least 15 to 20 years comfortable to us.

items.statement: Disclosure policy amended to comply fully with SEBI LODR regulations
items.quote: This is based on the SEBI regulation, LODR regulations, we wanted to comply with in full. So, accordingly, we amended our disclosure requirements as a part of our corporate governance.

items.statement: Force majeure invoked on GSPC gas supply shortfall; dispute resolution ongoing, no penalty expected
items.quote: In all of our gas sales contract, there is a force majeure clause. The force majeure clause is very wide, which talks about not only cyclone, and any disruption to our top-side facility and our reservoir issues would be construed and termed as a force majeure.

items.statement: Talent pool reasonably increased to meet growth targets
items.quote: We have reasonably increased our talent pool to meet our growth targets.

items.statement: Dirok gas grid connection line half completed; expected within 6 months (Oct-Nov 2024)
items.quote: It should be within six months.

items.statement: PY-3 stake (21%) retained; will re-engage if economical
items.quote: In our mind, we still hold and we believe we are holding 21% of the participating interest in the block. As at the moment, there is no progress to us and if they come out of the details of what has been done, so we will decide whether to get back into that or not.

items.statement: Operating cash flow ~Rs 300+ cr to fund capital investments
items.quote: You could have seen we have about 300 plus operating cash flow that will be pumped into our capital investments.

items.statement: Volume growth expected to continue from Q4 FY24 base quarter-on-quarter in FY25
items.quote: Yes, Nirav, should happen over that.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to stabilize as recession tapers off and Chinese domestic demand improves
items.quote: As far as the EBITDA margin is concerned, it is an ongoing thing because we hope this condition stabilizes. We hope that the Chinese domestic parameters also improve.

items.statement: Rs. 250 crore expansion at Dahej site for rubber chemical capacities approved and work begun
items.quote: As part of our strategic roadmap to continue to expand our market presence, all of you will be aware of our board approval for Rs. 250 crore investment at our Dahej site for further expansion of our rubber chemical capacities. We have begun work on the same.

items.statement: New capacity expected to start commercial activity in second half of FY26-27
items.quote: We actually we have said in 2.5 years we'll be commissioning it and it depends on the approvals post thereafter from the customers. While we expect our endeavor is to complete faster, so maybe in FY26-27 some part of the last second half or later half something like that you can expect to start commercial activity from the same.

items.statement: Overall utilization at 65% but individual products at different stages with some at 95-100%
items.quote: Yes, so while we have always mentioned that 65% number that you mentioned is an overall number, while at an individual product level, we could be at different stages. So, and some could be at 95 and 100, and then we do the usual de-bottlenecking and stretch it to the maximum possible.

items.statement: FY24 export volume growth 9% year-on-year despite geopolitical tensions
items.quote: For Financial Year '24, we have recorded a year-on-year volume growth of 9% in our export segment, despite the challenges posed by geopolitical tensions and fluctuating raw material prices.

items.statement: FY24 overall volume growth 2% with domestic flattish and exports 9%
items.quote: For FY24, the overall volume growth is about 2%. I think the domestic was flattish and export is 9% and I think we have already addressed the question of the other products in exports, the Latex market where this year we have seen some marginal improvement not great from the FY23 numbers, so in that sense the growth is more out of non-Latex rubber chemicals.

items.statement: Indian tyre industry expected to grow mid-single digits in current financial year
items.quote: As per the market reports, the Indian tyre industry is expected to grow in the mid-single digits in the current financial year on the back of a stable growth in the replacement segment and growing segment for OEMs in the passenger vehicle and two-wheeler segments.

items.statement: Chinese dumping expected to continue until domestic consumption in China picks up
items.quote: I think it's also a factor of how much the domestic consumption in China picks up and I think until then they're going to be looking at markets to push their products or dump their products and I think it will stay on unless domestic volumes pick up.

items.statement: Management senses margins have bottomed out and should not go further below current levels
items.quote: Yes, so this was something one of the earlier questions, and we get the sense that it's kind of bottomed out and should not go further below this.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 selling price dropped 6.5% quarter-on-quarter with corresponding drop in raw material prices
items.quote: Selling price has dropped by 6.5% on a Q-o-Q basis. Volumes for Q4 FY24 have shown a healthy growth of 12% on a Q-o-Q basis.

items.statement: Aniline and MIBK prices moved up recently but finished goods prices tend to move with raw material momentum
items.quote: Yes, so typically with momentum raw material prices, also the finished goods prices tend to move and it also plays on the supply demand situation. Yes, you're right, Aniline prices did move up. But it's kind of been a bit up and down in the last few weeks due to different macro environment reasons. But we see that with the cost moving up, the prices also can be realized.

items.statement: Latex specialty volumes degrew ~40% from FY22 to FY24 (index from 100 to 50-60) but other products showing growth
items.quote: You can say if the index was 100 in FY22, today it's probably at around 50, 60. So, there is a 40% degrowth. But what is happening is on the other products, on the other products we have actually started showing signs of growth in other regular products and other specialties as well.

items.statement: Latex specialty volumes expected to recover gradually from 60 to 65 index in FY25
items.quote: We cannot expect to recover back to 100. The 60 will go gradually to 65, thereabout something like that.

items.statement: Q4 volume growth from both existing and new customers, roughly uniformly distributed
items.quote: So, I would not be able to put my finger on a specific number if I split the growth, but I would say it's kind of more or less uniformly distributed.

items.statement: Strategic engagements with global customers gaining traction and new businesses added in last few months
items.quote: As indicated in our previous calls, our strategic initiatives and engagement with global strategic customers has started gaining traction. For Financial Year '24, we have recorded a year-on-year volume growth of 9% in our export segment, despite the challenges posed by geopolitical tensions and fluctuating raw material prices.

items.statement: China plus one strategy and supply reliability driving customer preference for non-Chinese sources
items.quote: But our clear value proposition, which our customers see from somebody like a supplier of NOCIL is one is the China de-risking strategy which is China plus one and they're looking at long-term supply reliability. So, for some of the products outside of China, there are very other few players who are really kind of making some of these products.

items.statement: Utility costs reduced 15-20% through price benefits and efficiency measures during FY24
items.quote: So, while then it's a combination of also certain price benefits on the utility per unit basis, but also efficiency measures coming in, I would say roughly around 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Power cogeneration investments expected to add further benefits as volumes increase
items.quote: There is expected to be benefit because we are also working on power core generation and so that's also going to add to it as we keep increasing our volumes.

items.statement: Freight cost increases not significant and mitigated through customer discussions
items.quote: Also, I think it's not very significant, and we've also been able to discuss with customers on how this can be mitigated. So, that's also kind of played in. We don't see any significant impact on account of that.

items.statement: Export contribution ~33-34% of Q4 FY24 revenue, similar to ~30-32% for full year FY24
items.quote: Yes, it's about 33% for the quarter, 33%, 34%.

items.statement: Chinese capacity additions in accelerators and antioxidants continue but NOCIL sees demand growth in specific products
items.quote: The market growth in terms of the specific products that we're looking at continues to be on a positive trend. And there are markets where we can continue to grow with these products, not only a bit more in the domestic, but also in the international market.

items.statement: Diversification into new chemistries underway but no specific timeline; rubber chemical growth plans unaffected
items.quote: Yes, yes, we're looking at it, again, alluding to the earlier question versus under progress on that front, Aditya.

items.statement: Operational excellence initiatives in manufacturing driving utility efficiencies
items.quote: You may recall also, Nirav, in one of the last calls we were talking about operational excellence initiatives in manufacturing and this is coming from our utilities, benefits that we have looked at efficiencies and areas to improve. So, that is actually showing up in the other expenses coming now.

items.statement: Expect steady growth recovery in USA and continued robust demand from Asia and India in FY25
items.quote: As we progress through financial year 2025, we anticipate a steady growth recovery in the USA and continued robust demand from Asia and especially India.

items.statement: Important contracts formalized in FY24 and promising business pipeline with OEMs
items.quote: With important contracts formalized during financial year 2024, we also have a promising business pipeline with OEMs.

items.statement: Acquired new property for forward integration and assembly line expansion
items.quote: To prepare for our growth, we recently acquired a new property, providing sufficient headroom for forward integration and expansion of our assembly lines.

items.statement: Proposed wholly owned subsidiary in Italy to enhance European presence
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that we have proposed to incorporate a wholly owned subsidiary in Italy.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 PAT margin improved 551 bps to 22.66% due to input cost control and operational efficiency
items.quote: For Q4 FY '24, our profit after tax surged by 34.07% to INR25.33 crores, with the tax margin improving by 551 basis points to 22.66 %.

items.statement: Bimetal gross margin 40-42%, shunt gross margin 45-48%, 3-5% EBITDA delta between products
items.quote: So generally, the gross margin comes out in bimetal is around 40 %-42% and that's why the EBITDA level is lower, since in shunt register, the gross margin is around 45%-48%.

items.statement: USA degrowth due to sluggish automotive, EV slowdown, inventory correction and election wait-and-watch
items.quote: The degrowth is directly linked to what we've discussed in the past as well in several calls that the automotive market is sluggish. The EV market hasn't really moved at the pace at which the market and the OEMs had anticipated and because of which end of 2023 and 2024 has been a year where most of the OEMs have been kind of busy correcting their inventories and that's where we've seen a degrowth

items.statement: Europe thermostatic bimetal trimetals grew 25.79% in FY24
items.quote: In Europe, we achieved a 25.79 % growth in thermostatic bimetal trimetals sales for financial year '24, maintaining a stable performance across both segments.

items.statement: India thermostatic bimetal trimetals grew 31.69% YoY in FY24
items.quote: In India, our thermostatic bimetal trimetals sales grew by 31.69% year-on-year, effectively offsetting the sluggish demand from the Americas.

items.statement: Asia ex-India shunt register sales grew 32.84% YoY in FY24
items.quote: Asia, excluding India, also saw an increase of 32.84% year-on-year in shunt register sales, reinforcing our expanding market presence.

items.statement: Smart meter demand in India geared up for substantial growth starting FY25
items.quote: The domestic market is now pretty geared up to start deploying these smart meters into the market and we are expecting substantially good growth starting this financial year.

items.statement: Shunt revenue split: 80% automotive, 14% energy meter, 4% gas metering; metering expected minimum 2x growth
items.quote: About 80% of our revenue in shunt comes from automotive applications, about 14% comes from the energy meter applications and some of that also comes through gas metering applications, which is about 4%, the balance. Going forward, as I had mentioned earlier, when it comes to automotive, we feel that this year, it might be flat. However, when it comes to metering, we are looking at a minimum of 2x.

items.statement: Bimetal: >80% switchgear, customers like ABB, Schneider forecasting 2x-3x growth in 3-4 years
items.quote: The kind of growth that we are seeing there and the forecast that we are receiving from our major switchgear players like large companies like ABB, Schneider, etc, the kind of forecast that they're giving us is, you know, 2x to 3x in the next three years, four years.

items.statement: Ready with more than 3x existing output capacity for bimetal growth
items.quote: We are actually ready with more than 3x our existing output.

items.statement: Final stages of due diligence with French company Metalor for JV; expect completion within FY25
items.quote: We are in the now finishing stages of due diligence with the French company, Metalor, that has appointed PWC for the due diligence purpose. We are in the final stages of that. Now, we are awaiting a report. Actually, Metalor is awaiting a report of the due diligence. And then, the further steps will obviously emerge from what comes out of the due diligence. But we are guessing that the timeframe f

items.statement: Metalor JV targets margin improvement to 14-15% via silver alloy control and forward integration

items.statement: Won international orders: Rs 120 cr Saudi Arabia water treatment plant, Rs 250 cr UAE project
items.quote: we've got significant orders from Saudi Arabia, which is for setting up a water treatment plant, including demineralization plant. This is roughly around Rs. 120 crores. The other one, is from UAE and that value is roughly in the range of Rs. 250 crores.

items.statement: Chemical volumes picking up sequentially from international markets, expected to continue
items.quote: There has been a sequential pickup in the volumes from the international market and we anticipate this to continue over the coming quarters also. That's what has led to the recovery in the top line.

items.statement: Chemical margins stable but seeing cost impact from Middle East situation and higher shipping times
items.quote: The margins have remained stable, and that's because of the continuing environment of stable prices. But we are seeing a bit of an impact over the last maybe few months due to the situation in the Middle East, which has impacted costs to some extent, and also the shipping times have gone up.

items.statement: Chemical volumes expected to improve over coming year, margins maintainable at current levels if raw material prices stable
items.quote: Overall, we do see that the volumes in the business would continue to improve over the coming year. And margins also if all things remain equal in terms of the global environment, in terms of the raw material prices, we should be able to maintain the current level and round about these levels.

items.statement: Engineering margins hit by revenue shortfall vs expectations, one domestic EPC contract with unforeseen cost increases, and subsidiary infrastructure spend ahead of revenue
items.quote: The Engineering margins have suffered during the current year in the quarter under review. We have seen some dip in the overall revenue numbers as compared to our expectations. There has also been one specific contract where we have witnessed unforeseen cost increases. This is a domestic industrial EPC job and that has impacted the overall margins significantly.

items.statement: Engineering margin drag from problem contract to continue 1-2 quarters, then improve with higher execution volumes
items.quote: This one contract where we have witnessed unforeseen price increases, we expect the drag would continue for maybe 1 to 2 quarters. And thereafter things should improve significantly. And margins would also improve because the overall volume of execution during the year would go up.

items.statement: Working capital levels structurally higher due to EPC revenue share increase and Sri Lanka contract advance run-off, to remain at FY23-24 levels
items.quote: Going forward, we expect that the working capital level to be largely in line with what we have been shown at FY '23 March and also what we are showing now at FY '24. We will have these kinds of levels of working capital because as the EPC segment invoicing and the share in the overall revenue increases, we will have this kind of working capital levels going forward.

items.statement: Mapril contributed Rs 92 cr revenue for full year FY24, consolidated under Chemical segment with lower margins than standalone
items.quote: On an overall basis for the full year, the revenue impact of Mapril is in the region of around Rs. 92 crores.

items.statement: Mapril margins lower than standalone Chemical segment margins
items.quote: Margins of Mapril, are lower than what we have seen for the Chemical segment in the standalone.

items.statement: Engineering order book execution timeline roughly 2 years on average, some international jobs shorter
items.quote: This should be roughly around a 2-year period for some of the significant contracts which have been declared on the stock exchange. A couple of the large international jobs have much shorter period of execution. But on an average, it would be fair to say roughly a 2-year period.

items.statement: Engineering growth guidance for FY25 at 15-20%, at least matching FY24 growth
items.quote: And I would expect that the growth should be at least what we saw last year. And at the same time, I would only want to give you a subdued projection of roughly around 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Engineering consolidated PBIT margin FY24 7.7% vs 9.1% in FY23, expect to return to at least 9.1% in FY25
items.quote: On a consol basis, we saw for the full year roughly 7.7% margin. And for FY '22-'23, this number was around 9.1%. And we do expect that we will at least come back to that level.

items.statement: UP contract execution expected to complete by end of FY25 after election process
items.quote: We are expecting by the end of this financial year that contract should be executed, and we await the resumption of pace after the election process has been completed.

items.statement: Merger of Global Composites and Ion Exchange Environment Management completed in Q4 FY24, Ion Exchange Project Engineering merger withdrawn for refiling
items.quote: The company's merger process with 2 of its Indian subsidiaries, namely Global Composites and Structural Limited and Ion Exchange Environment Management Limited was successfully completed during this quarter. The merger application of Ion Exchange project and Engineering Limited was withdrawn by the company and will be considered for refiling in due course of time.

items.statement: Engineering division margins adversely impacted by unforeseen cost increase on one significant domestic contract
items.quote: There was one significant contract where we saw an unforeseen cost increase, and we had to, therefore, take that extra cost provision in our books. That has led to an adverse impact on the margins reported by the Engineering division.

items.statement: Total capex for current year around Rs. 115 crores, largely for Roha resin expansion
items.quote: The total Capex, for the current year is in the region of, Rs. 115 crores. largely the capex is into the Roha plant which we are currently undertaking for our resin expansion..

items.statement: Roha plant capex around Rs. 50 crores for the year, cumulative spend around Rs. 70 crores
items.quote: Roha, I can share that for the year, the capex is around Rs. 50 crores. And cumulatively, we have spent around Rs. 70 crores.

items.statement: Overall Roha project capex just under Rs. 400 crores, majority to be spent in current year
items.quote: Yes. We have indicated earlier also the overall Capex for the Roha is just under Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: Roha project capex spend this year expected around Rs. 250-300 crores
items.quote: We can't be very definitive about that as of today, but it should be around that number of Rs. 250 crores to Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Normalized working capital level expected around 70-75 days
items.quote: So the normalized level, if I understood your question correctly, should be in the region of around 70 to 75 days.

items.statement: Current total working capital at 99 days, receivables around 154 days
items.quote: The total working capital in terms of days will be 99 days. 99 days for receivables? The total receivables will be in the region of around 154 days

items.statement: Chemical segment margins expected at similar levels if stable prices and geopolitical dynamics continue
items.quote: As far as the Chemical segment is concerned, we should be seeing margins at similar levels as of date, provided that we continue to witness stable prices and the overall dynamics on the geopolitical side do not alter significantly.

items.statement: International order book 27% as of March 2024 end
items.quote: International order book as of March '24 end is around 27%.

items.statement: Roha project financing: 20% internal accruals, 80% debt
items.quote: No, as regards financing of the Roha project, 20% of that will be from internal accruals and balance will be debt.

items.statement: Roha facility total investment includes Rs. 125 crores backward integration, asset turnover ~2x on Rs. 275 crores
items.value: 125 crores backward integration, 2x asset turnover on 275 crores
items.quote: Total investment includes capex for backward integration of roughly 125 crores and asset turnover of around 2 times should be calculated on the figure of 275 crores.

items.statement: Employee cost as percentage of sales to drop significantly once project execution scales up
items.quote: As a percentage of sales it will go down quite a bit, and that's the reason I mentioned that there is a bit of an overhang of the expenditure that we are making on infrastructure, including build-up of manpower. Once we see the project execution comes back to the levels where we expect them to, the percentages will drop significantly.

items.statement: Consumer segment employee cost run rate of Rs. 80-81 crores to continue
items.quote: But we will see the run rate of Rs. 80 crores, Rs. 81 crores, going ahead also? Yes, that's right.

items.statement: India engineering market size (ex-municipal) estimated at Rs. 20,000-25,000 crores per year, international many times larger
items.value: Rs. 20,000 crores to Rs. 25,000 crores per year
items.quote: So if we exclude the municipal segment and also the purely similar construction-oriented jobs coming from the government, we would expect the market size in India to be in the range of around Rs. 20,000 crores to Rs. 25,000 crores per year. And if you look at the international market, this is many times over of this number.

items.statement: Focus geographies for engineering opportunities: Middle East, Southeast Asia, Africa
items.quote: The geographies which we focus on is the Middle East, the Southeast of Asia and the African region, which is wh ere I feel a lot of the engineering opportunities will come for us

items.statement: Consumer segment delivered ~31% growth current year, expects similar growth momentum
items.quote: You would have seen that we have delivered roughly around 31% growth for the current year. And we do expect that we would maintain momentum in a similar range of growth.

items.statement: Engineering segment expects 15-20% growth given healthy order book, no formal guidance given
items.quote: And given that we are carrying a very healthy order growth, 15% to 20% growth, we will certainly hope to achieve, if not more.

items.statement: Chemical segment margins sustainable if stable raw material pricing and geopolitical environment continue
items.quote: we have benefited from a stable raw mat erial pricing for the last few quarters. And we have also not witnessed any significant variations in the exchange rates or significant negative impact because of the geopolitical scenario, which has remained as it is. This is what has helped us to maintain the margin levels. If we are going to see a stable environment in the future also, the margin levels a

items.statement: Customer advances Rs. 180 crores, unearned revenue Rs. 224 crores as of March end
items.quote: The customer advance as of March end was around Rs. 180 crores and the unearned revenue was around Rs. 224 crores.

items.statement: Company participates very selectively in UP-type projects, sees more such projects coming in ensuing period
items.quote: These type of projects have been executed across the country and we have just taken a very small portion of it. we would see more of these coming in the ensuing period and we have been very, very selective in participating in project of this nature, and that's going to be our strength in the future also. We will participate very selectively.

items.statement: Regulatory pressure to improve industrial water/waste treatment infrastructure driving engineering opportunities
items.quote: there is also a regulatory pressure to improve the industrial infrastructure to treat the water and the waste. Therefore, we do hope that we will be able to get a lot of orders from the various parts or the various segments of the market

items.statement: Targets 25-30% annual AUM growth, AUM >INR500 cr by FY25 and INR600 cr by FY26
items.quote: Way forward, we aim to achieve a 25% to 30% annual increase in A UM, with targets surpassing INR500 crores by financial year 2025 and we aim to reach INR600 crores loan book by FY '26

items.statement: Targets 75 branches by end of FY25
items.quote: By the end of financial year '25, we aspire to establish a total of 75 branches, enhancing our market presence and accessibility.

items.statement: Expects 20-25% growth in P&L and interest income in FY25
items.quote: We are seeing around 20% to 25% growth in the coming year as well, both on the P&L and the income.

items.statement: Targets INR200 cr fresh disbursement and net AUM addition of ~INR120 cr in FY25
items.quote: AUM, yes, definitely we are targeting to add, to disburse around INR200 crores of fresh disbursement this year. And with the rundown every month that we have of principal via collections and closures, we should be adding around INR120-odd crores of fresh AUM to the existing.

items.statement: Expects gross NPA to decline 25-30 bps by end of FY25
items.quote: And we have about 2.6% NPA, gross NPA that we have reported this year with a very comfortable provisional coverage on that. And net NPA is 0.36%. So we have done a very conservative approach there and we do n't see further slippages there. In fact, with the addition in the AUM, this number should come down by 25 to 30 basis points by end of this

items.statement: Plans to migrate NPA recognition from 150 days to 120 days by Mar'25 and 90 days by Mar'26
items.quote: So this is a 150 cut off number. And as per RBI, we have a couple of more years to come down to 90 days and be at par with larger NBFCs and banks. So this year, we'll be going ahead and closing March '25 at 120 days and March '26 at 90 days.

items.statement: Targets revenue of INR80-85 cr in FY25
items.quote: To be honest, INR100 crores looks tough, but total revenue should be around INR80 crores-INR85 crores at a conservative approach.

items.statement: Branch setup cost INR2-3 lakh per branch; breakeven at INR3.5-4 cr AUM in 4-5 months
items.quote: So yes the expansion of newer geographies has happened this year, but to be very hone st our branches are not very grand where we are splur ging on the IT or infra of the branch. So typically INR2 lakh to INR3 lakh per branch is what the early cost is and then 3 months to 4 months of hiring and I mean till the branch becomes viable on its ow n and the team joins in and there is a INR4 crores to IN

items.statement: Opened 7-8 branches in last 4-5 months; total 45 branches; plans 7-8 new branches in FY25 including 4-5 in Maharashtra
items.quote: We have opened around 7 to 8 branches in last 4 to 5 months. So that expansion has been already done. This year, we will target to open 3 to 4 branches in the ne w state that we are targeting, mostly Maharashtra. And apart from that, I think should P&L and the total interest income should see around 20% to 25% growth.

items.statement: Plans 4-5 branches in Maharashtra next quarter or Q3 FY25; spoke locations near existing branches in Gujarat and MP
items.quote: Once we close that within a couple of months we'll be able to shut down on a few locations and open about 4 locations to 5 locations in Maharashtra in the current financial year.

items.statement: AUM grew 22.31% to INR368 cr in FY24; vehicle loans 19.5%, mortgage 80.5% of AUM
items.quote: Our AUM sur ged to almost INR368 crores, making an impressive growth of 22.31% compared to the previous year. The substantial increase reflects our strong performance and the trust bestowed upon by our clients.

items.statement: FY24 disbursement INR179 cr; MSME+LAP disbursement INR110 cr, vehicle loans INR68-69 cr
items.quote: Our disbursement reached to about – reached to INR179 crores in Financial Year '24.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 62.72%, net profit margin 19.47%; Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 57.88%
items.quote: In financial year '24, the company showed strong financial growth, with total revenues reaching INR66.36 crores, up by 19.07%. The company's EBITDA inc reased by 30% to INR41.62 crores, with a notable EBITDA margin of 62.72%. Net profit rose to INR12.92 crores, making a significant 24.59% increase, resulting in a net profit margin of 19.47%.

items.statement: NIM stable at 10.5-11%; cost of borrowings ~11.75-12%, expected to drop 25 bps in FY25
items.quote: NIMs are around 10.5 t o 11% which have been stable and marginally improved. We see the same kind of NIMs going forward as well. Little bit improvement could be seen if we are able to add a good amount of two -wheeler loan, three -wheeler loan, vehicle loan and electric vehicles portfolio

items.statement: MSME/LAP lending rates 16.5-24%, average portfolio yield ~19.5%; vehicle loans yield higher than mortgage
items.quote: We started about 16% and go to roughly 22%, 23% average yield on our portfolio comes to about 19.5%, 20% and competitive advantage that we see with us is having tested the portfolio and performance very minutely in a couple of Black Swan events that have happened recently number one.

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.6%, net NPA 0.36% in FY24; collection efficiency 95.5%; MP/Gujarat portfolio 99% in current/zero buckets
items.quote: And we have about 2.6% NPA, gross NPA that we have reported this year with a very comfortable provisional coverage on that. And net NPA is 0.36%. So we have done a very conservative approach there and we do n't see further slippages

items.statement: Collection efficiency improved from 70-75% during COVID to 95.5% in FY24
items.quote: Roughly NPA is 2.5%. Collection efficiency on the entire book comes to about 95% -- has been 95.5% last year and this has significantly improved in the last 3 years to 4 years. It has -- we have seen this collection efficiency close to 75%, 70% also in the lockdown period.

items.statement: Borrowings INR242 cr, up 41% YoY; leverage 1.4x (net worth INR167 cr); capital adequacy ~46%; added PSU banks, scheduled banks, SFBs
items.quote: Additionally, our total borrowings escalated to INR242 cr ores, showcasing a notable 41% surge over the preceding year, in which we have added small finance banks and few commercial banks, increasing our share of lending from banks.

items.statement: Plans to issue NCDs soon; currently funded via term loans and working capital limits from banks/NBFCs
items.quote: Apart from that, we are also thinking of issuance of NCDs very soon. But as of now, it's completely through banks and NBFCs via the mode of term loans or small working capital limits from a couple of banks.

items.statement: Rights issue deferred by board; will reconsider at appropriate time after AUM reaches ~INR500 cr
items.quote: So we have given intimation for the rights issue, but later we deferred this agenda. The proposal was placed for the Board of Directors, but the management along with the Independent Directors of the company were in the opinion to defer the proposal of issuance of rights issue at a later date and for consideration at an appropriate time.

items.statement: Key hires for MP, Gujarat, Maharashtra joining in 40-45 days; MP team from large NBFCs with nil attrition; attrition rising in Rajasthan
items.quote: We have hired a few key positions and they will be joining the company in about 40 to 45 days from now. So by June end, our key hiring will be done for the financial year. And teams below them will join in the next quarter.

items.statement: Attrition risk in older Rajasthan geographies; stable teams in new MP/Gujarat branches
items.quote: One of the risks that we foresee is higher attrition in our employees, which is in the older geographies, not in the new geographies. The team has been stable for around 15 to 18 months with us in MP and now Gujarat. But in the older geographie s, there has been an uptrend of attrition

items.statement: MP/Gujarat portfolio targets better customer profiles, not first-time borrowers; 99% collection efficiency in current/zero buckets
items.quote: Yes, the portfolio is performing much better. The yield is a little bit lesser because as far as we are going from Jaipur, we are concentrating on a better profile of customers. And we are not targeting first time borrowers and new to credit customers there as of now. So that has given an additional comfort to the portfolio. And we have close to 99% of colle ction efficiency and portfolio in the c

items.statement: Competitive advantage: tested portfolio through black swan events, lean hierarchy for faster turnaround, proprietary internal scoring module
items.quote: Number two we in the management team have been working with the people at our ground with feet on street have visited a lot of customers, done their interaction PD, FIA on our own. So we understand what the customer is actually demanding and thirdly we have a lean hierarchy. So our turnaround times are much faster than larger NBFCs and banks where if there are any deviations or waivers then the ch

items.statement: ROE 6-7% due to low leverage (1.4x vs industry 2-3x); expects ROE improvement as leverage increases to 2-3x
items.quote: I think you answered the question on my part and it's definitely because of the low leverage. If you compare us to larger other NBFCs, gen erally, all the NBFCs are 2 to 2.5, 3x leveraged and have a capital ad equacy of around 20 %-25%. But we're sitting at 45%.

items.statement: Current capital commitment at 65-70 crore as of call date
items.quote: We have already made significant progress towards this, with almost 65 to 70 crores as of today.

items.statement: Raised 15 crore NCD fully committed, expects allocation within 30 days
items.quote: Regarding the fundraise, I am sure some of you saw our announcement on the Bombay Stock Exchange about raising an NCD worth about 15 crores. We have been blown away by the response from subscribers. From a commitment perspective, it is already committed, and we believe the entire 15 crores will be allocated within the next 30 days.

items.statement: Plans to raise more NCD cohorts to support growth
items.quote: Post that, we will explore new cohorts of NCDs because we see tremendous growth.

items.statement: Disbursements jumped 4x from Q1-Q2 (17-18 crore) to Q3-Q4 (90 crore) FY24
items.quote: If we look at the disbursement of lo ans and compare Q1 and Q2, which was almost 17-18 crores, to Q3 and Q4, which combined is almost 90 crores, we see a 4x jump in the amount of loans disbursed

items.statement: Expects DPD to improve significantly below 2.8% in coming quarters
items.quote: This gives us confidence that future numbers will be much better, potentially lower than the current 2.8%.

items.statement: Co-lending revenue lower than LSP model but PBT/PAT unchanged; ROI same
items.quote: In a co-lending model, the revenue which Apollo can earn is lower than the LSP model, but from a bottom-line perspective, both of them are exactly the same because in both these models, the ROI that Apollo is earning is exactly the same.

items.statement: Expects significantly better ROE in FY25 due to better capital deployment and attractive NCD rates
items.quote: Obviously, compared to last year, I'm expecting this year for us to have significantly better ROEs, largely because when I compare it to last year versus this year, obviously this year we're expecting our capital to be significantly well deployed.

items.statement: Charges partners 16.5-18% ROI on capital commitment
items.quote: So the capital commitment, you know, ROI that we basically typically charge could be anywhere between 16.5% to 18%. That's typically the range of ROI that a polo charges.

items.statement: Partner NBFCs include Branch, Cashi, True Credits; LSPs include OKCredit, Jar
items.quote: Just to name a few partners we have on board and had in the last financial year: from an NBFC standpoint, we have Branch, Cashi, and True Credits. From an LSP standpoint, meaning non-regulated partners, we have some amazing partners like OKCredit and Jar.

items.statement: Many partner NBFCs have AUM over 1,000 crore and commit capital for 1+ years
items.quote: Many of the NBFCs we collaborate with have AuMs upwards of 1,000 crores. That's testament to the fact that, despite being systematically important NBFCs, despite all of those things, they are choosing to work with Apolo.

items.statement: Team of 30 people, may grow to 35 despite AUM ramp-up
items.quote: Despite the ramp -up in terms of AUM, which will continue this year, t he number of employees will not change much. Maybe we'll go from 30 to 35 people, but I don't foresee a significant change in terms of employees

items.statement: RBI digital lending guidelines and 5% FLDG cap triggered partner re-evaluation and shift to NBFCs
items.quote: There was no bigger change to the Apollo business model than the cap on FLDG, which was made to be 5%. The minute that 5% cap happened, we had to reevaluate the kind of people, in term s of loan service providers (LSPs), that we were working with

items.statement: RBI risk weight increase on unsecured loans creates opportunity due to Apollo's low debt-to-equity headroom
items.quote: Today, the good news for Apollo is the headroom is so high. Realistically, we could go from a debt-to-equity perspective of easily 2 to 3x very smoothly from this point in time onwards.

items.statement: Shifted capital allocation from LSPs to digital NBFCs; co-lending model now majority
items.quote: If you compare FY23 to FY24, FY23 primarily had our entire capital commitment comin g from non -regulated LSP partners. Now, most of it is coming from digital lending partners, which is a big shift for us

items.statement: Loan ticket size under 2 lakh, tenure 3-12 months is sweet spot
items.quote: So we like to do loans which are probably less than a couple of lakhs in terms of ticket size, and we also like to keep the duration usually in the 3 to 12-month range.

items.statement: Capital commitment 65-70 crore as of call date; earns interest on committed amount regardless of utilization
items.quote: As of today, we have a scoreboard inside the company. The capital commitment that we have is almost 65 crores. We expect that by the first half of this year, H1, we expect that number to be 100 crores. So 100 crores of capital commitment means we'll be ear ning interest on 100 crores for a period of 12

items.statement: Net worth approximately 60 crore as of call date
items.quote: I think, you know, I am not 120% sure of the numbers. But last I checked, our network was about 60 odd crores.

items.statement: Q4 PBT lower due to one-time write-off of pre-DLG delinquent loans; will improve ECL provisioning
items.quote: Basically, what has happened is that our write-off policy was such that all our pre-DLG and previous year delinquent loans were reflected in the March quarter when we decided to write them off. So, just so you know, this is the first time we've truly written off loans, and the impact of that is what we are seeing in our Q4.

items.statement: No plans to offer tech as SaaS; considers technology a competitive moat
items.quote: we really believe technology is our secret sauce, right? And we are not at all interested in actually giving it out to any other NDFC because honestly, it would make them as efficient as us. And you know, why would you give away your secret sauce, right? Essential ly, so we don't have any motivation to do that at all

items.statement: Data stored on AWS India servers per RBI data localization requirements; backups on multiple servers
items.quote: RBI actually already came out with this in their original digital lending guidelines that you cannot store data outside India. So everybody pretty much in the fintech space has already, I mean, whatever server they're using, right? They're using the India version of that, right? So even our data, by the way, is stored inside India, in AWS servers which they've hosted inside India, specifically.

items.statement: Management targets average EBITDA margin of INR7 per liter for bulk alcohol business (ENA and ethanol combined) over the cycle
items.quote: Going forward, we believe that the bulk business, which is a combination of ENA and ethanol, our EBITDA margins in this business will be at around INR7 a liter.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 bulk alcohol EBITDA margin collapsed to near zero due to FCI rice supply discontinuation and open market rice price spike
items.quote: Frankly, there were no spreads. That's why you saw the kind of performance that you see.

items.statement: Management expects bulk alcohol margins to recover to average INR7 per liter by end of FY25 as maize crop arrives and rice prices soften
items.quote: In fact, I believe that -- by the end of this year, we will be back to our average level of margins that we have seen in the last few years, which is around INR7 per liter.

items.statement: Ethanol production shifting from rice to maize; currently over 2/3 of ethanol output expected from maize in FY25 versus negligible in FY24
items.quote: In this financial year, for ethanol, we expect over 2/3 of our ethanol production to come from maize?

items.statement: Total installed capacity now 300 million liters per year after regulatory approvals for Jharkhand and West Bengal 60 KLPD expansions
items.quote: After certain pending regulatory approvals were complete in Q4, our total installed capacity pending regulatory approvals for Jharkhand and West Bengal expansion that is, our total installed capacity now stands at 300 million liters per year.

items.statement: Bengal and Jharkhand 60 KLPD plants to add INR215-230 crores incremental revenue in FY25; UP bottling plant commissioned in April for own brands
items.quote: Bengal and Jharkhand, 60 KLPD will give you an additional revenue of anything between INR215 crores to INR230 crores.

items.statement: Prestige & Above segment volume grew 170% YoY in Q4 FY24 to 0.13 million cases; full year volume 0.38 million cases, up 84% YoY
items.quote: the quarter gone by, we witnessed a sales volume of 0.13 million cases with a growth of 170%. For the full year, also the performance has been robust. Our full year volumes stood at 0.38 million cases with a growth of 84% year -on-year

items.statement: Regular & Others segment volume grew 8% YoY in Q4 FY24 to 3.43 million cases; full year volume 14.16 million cases, profitability INR1,404 million up 22% YoY
items.quote: For the full year, this number of volume stands at 14.16 million and profitability at INR1,404 million with 22% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Launching Mountain Oak and SNOSKI Vodka in Prestige & Above; RTD brand Not Out launched in Delhi; expanding distribution from 6 to 8 states in FY25
items.quote: We are also going to be expanding our distribution presence, which currently stands at 6 states to another 2 states during the coming quarters.

items.statement: Joint venture with ANSA McAL for Carib Beer distribution and contract manufacturing in India; launch expected Q1 FY26; no brewery investment until 1-2 million cases scale
items.quote: We plan to contract manufacture the beer in India to start with, and we expect launch in Q1 of FY'26.

items.statement: Net debt increased to INR241 crores at end of FY24 from INR194 crores in FY23 due to new units and geographies
items.quote: Our net debt of cash -- net of cash and cash equivalents at the end of FY'25 stands at INR241 crores, a slight increase versus FY'23, which stood at INR194 crores.

items.statement: Income tax demand of INR40.93 crores received; INR30.41 crores deposited in protest and appeal filed; management believes no provision needed
items.quote: Subsequent to the year-end, the company has received assessment orders of income tax. The amount of tax demand is INR40.93 crores out of which INR5.3 crores was deposited in Q3. For the balance amount, the company has deposited INR25.11 crores in protest and has gone for appeal.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 bulk alcohol production 64.8 million liters; sales 48.7 million liters; full year power and fuel cost INR245 crores
items.quote: The production in Q4 has been 64.8 million liters. Our power and fuel cost for the entire year has been INR245 crores.

items.statement: FY25 AUM target ₹780 crore; FY26 AUM target to cross ₹1,000 crore
items.quote: Talking about business projection s, for the financial year 2025, the target AUM is ₹780 crores, and for FY26, the target AUM will cross ₹1,000 crores

items.statement: FY25 equity raise target ₹50-100 crore
items.quote: In FY25, we target to raise equity funds between ₹50 crores and ₹100 crores.

items.statement: FY25 branch target 90 branches; FY26 target to cross 100 branches
items.quote: The targeted branch count for FY25 is 90 branches, and for FY26, we aim to cross 100 branches.

items.statement: FY25 average monthly disbursement target ₹30-35 crore; annual disbursement around ₹400 crore; AUM ₹700-780 crore
items.quote: Our previous year target was for average monthly disbursement of ₹ 25 crores. For this year, if we take an average of 25% for the branches, so our average monthly target will be between ₹30 crores to ₹35 crores. And our disbursement will be around ₹400 crores hence our loan book will increase around ₹200 crores. And the AUM will be between ₹700 crores to ₹780 crores.

items.statement: Plan to open 15 new branches in Q2 FY25 in south and Maharashtra; 10-15 branches in Q3 FY25
items.quote: We plan to open 15 new branches in Q2 in the south and Maharashtra regions and 10-15 branches in Q3.

items.statement: New branches in Maharashtra (two clusters of six each), Karnataka (six), Tamil Nadu (five), Telangana (three), Andhra Pradesh (three to four)
items.quote: These new branches include two clusters in Maharashtra, each comprising six branches, along with six branches in Karnataka, five in Tamil Nadu, three in Telangana, a nd three to four in Andhra Pradesh

items.statement: New branches typically take 4-6 months to reach break-even
items.quote: It typically takes 4-6 months to achieve break-even in these new branches.

items.statement: Net interest margin on gross loan book 11.29%; spread maintained at 11%
items.quote: The company has maintained a healthy spread of 11%. The net interest margin on the gross loan book stands at 11.29%.

items.statement: Average borrowing cost 11.13% in FY24 vs 10.82% in FY23 due to repo rate increases
items.quote: Due to the increase in the repo rate, our average borrowing cost is 11.13%, compared to 10.82% in the previous year.

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.29% (down from 2.50%); Net NPA 0.69% (up from 0.51%)
items.quote: The gross non-performing asset (NPA) ratio is 2.29%, down from 2.50% in the previous year, while the net NPA ratio is 0.69%, up from 0.51% last year.

items.statement: Total outstanding borrowing ₹491 crore (up from ₹357 crore); mix 49% banks, 39% FIs, 12% NHB
items.quote: The company's total outstanding borrowing is ₹491 crores which was ₹357 crores last year. with 49% from banks, 39% from financial institutions, and 12% from the National Housing Bank.

items.statement: CEO Archis Jain spends 20-22 days/month in field; team of 650-700 employees
items.quote: Our team consists of approximately 650 to 700 highly skilled individuals who are dedicated to our cause.

items.statement: Fintech model not applicable in housing finance due to need for property docs, valuation, legal reports; fewer HFCs in rural areas due to fieldwork
items.quote: In rural areas, there are relatively fewer housing finance companies due to the extensive fieldwork required. Additionally, the fintech model is not applicable in housing finance companies. Fintech typically operates in unsecured loans where property documents, valuation, legal reports, and technical aspects are not required.

items.statement: Conservative 50% LTV maintained to mitigate property depreciation risk; no increase planned despite rising property prices
items.quote: Maintaining a conservative LTV margin is crucial for enhancing collection efficiency. Exceeding the appropriate LTV ratio, such as r eaching 80% to 85%, poses risks, as property values can depreciate significantly if defaults occur

items.statement: Good monsoon does not increase prepayments; instead boosts business activity and financing demand
items.quote: Good monsoon conditions do not directly lead to increased prepayments. Instead, business activity tends to surge during favorable monsoon periods. As business activity rises, individuals may require additional financing.

items.statement: Bank transfer (BT) rate 8-10% of loan book; balanced inflow/outflow
items.quote: The bank transfer, commonly referred to as BT, typically ranges from 8% to 10%. The amount transferred out from our finance company is generally reciprocated by an equivalent sum from the recipient finance company.

items.statement: ALM position comfortable; liquid funds ₹82 crore including ₹17 crore undrawn
items.quote: The company's liquidity position remains strong, with liquid funds of ₹82 crores, including ₹17 crores of undrawn funds. Our asset-liability management (ALM) position is also comfortable.

items.statement: Favorable monsoon stimulates rural income and housing demand; but no certainty factored into guidance
items.quote: Sir, during a favorable monsoon season, development is stimulated across the entire country. Monsoon plays a pivotal role in India's economy due to its significant contribution to agriculture. With increased agricultural productivity, there is a correspond ing rise in income levels, prompting people to invest in housing, expand businesses, and foster overall development

items.statement: Fixed-rate loan book; repo rate increases cause temporary NIM pressure; rate cuts would improve profits
items.quote: Sir, our client base primarily opts for fixed-rate loans. If the repo rate rises, we might experience a slight profit decline for the fiscal year. However, if the repo rate subsequently decreases, our profits will likely increase.

items.statement: Recruited 10-12 branch managers for new branches; hired industry-experienced teams to minimize training time
items.quote: Business plans have been formulated, and teams have been recruited for these locations, including the appointment of 10 to 12 branch managers.

items.statement: Management expects non-engine/non-auto components to reach 25% of revenue in about a year, later than the earlier FY25 target.
items.quote: Yes, I don't think it would be possible in this current financial year, but perhaps a year later would be possible.

items.statement: Standalone business growth not expected to be double-digit immediately; significant new contracts to start production in next 12-24 months.
items.quote: I don't think double digits would be possible immediately in the coming quarters. But I think there will be a point where we have 3 or 4 new contracts that will come into SOP, or basically start supplies all in a very short period of time in the next 12 months to 24 months.

items.statement: EMOSS Europe growth will be muted over coming quarters due to recessionary environment.
items.quote: The growth at EMOSS would be muted over the coming quarters and should be taken into account considering the general economy in Europe.

items.statement: Retrofit EV business in India targets 20-25% gross margin and 10-15% operating margin at scale of 4,000-5,000 vehicles per year.
items.quote: At a big picture kind of long term goal if you ask me and we're talking about around a 20%, 25% gross margin and about a 15% operating margin 10% to 15% operating margin is what we hope for.

items.statement: OEM EV manufacturing in India is 2-3 years away, using retrofit powertrain data.
items.quote: It is still another two to three years away I would say.

items.statement: Domestic market expected to grow 8-10% YoY over next 3-4 years, helping offset export mix.
items.quote: The domestic market is expected to grow significantly over the next 3 years to 4 years, I would say, 8%, 9%, 10% year-on-year.

items.statement: EMOSS India has good traction with 15-20 large fleet customers owning over 10,000 LCVs combined.
items.quote: Just between them, they own or operate more than 10,000 vehicles just in the LCV category.

items.statement: EMOSS India signing commercial agreements with large waste collection, biomedical waste, and pan-India logistics providers.
items.quote: EMOSS India is in the process of signing commercial agreements with several key customers, including one of India's largest service provider company for the use in waste collection application, one of India's largest biomedical waste management company and an EV-only pan-India logistics provider.

items.statement: Standalone Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 17%, PAT margin 11%; domestic sales exceeded exports (53% vs 47%) lowering realizations.
items.quote: Total income for Q4 decreased by 0.2% year-on-year to INR176 crores. EBITDA margin was 17% and PAT margin was 11%.

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin ~10%, PAT margin ~1.2%.
items.quote: Coming to the consolidated business, total consol income decreased by about 8% to INR261 crores. EBITDA margin was about 10% and PAT margin was about 1.2%.

items.statement: New foundry and machine shop awards ensure full capacity utilization for next 4-5 years; new assembled camshaft plant in Solapur based on strong order book.
items.quote: In the last year, PCL has been awarded new business in the foundry as well as the machine shop that will ensure complete utilization of our capacities at least for the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: MEMCO secured additional business from key customers in fuel injection and critical instrumentation.
items.quote: MEMCO has already secured additional business from its key customers in the fuel injection business as well as critical instrumentation business.

items.statement: MFT Germany awarded new HVAC customer business for high-volume components starting production this calendar year.
items.quote: At MFT also, we have a new customer, which is in the HVAC space and has awarded us business for certain high-volume components that we will be starting production this year, this calendar year.

items.statement: PCL India ramped up non-engine brake component volumes; shipping commercially for last 2-3 months with higher volumes expected.
items.quote: We have ramped up the volume. Customer is already -- I mean, we're already shipping commercially to this customer for the last 2-3 months and we should see higher volumes in the coming year.

items.statement: Setting up new assembled camshaft plant in Solapur; adding new machining lines for new contracts starting production in 12-24 months.
items.quote: setting up a new assembled camshaft plant at a new location in Solapur, and these new investments are made on the basis of a strong order book for new assembled camshaft businesses that has been secured along with an addition of past camshaft business

items.statement: Retrofit satellite conversion workshops may open this financial year based on critical volume; currently outsourcing to partners.
items.quote: Yes, there could be a requirement to open a few centers in this financial year.

items.statement: PCL India cast 6.98M camshafts in FY24 vs 5.8M in FY23; machined 2.98M vs 3.1M.
items.quote: We cast 6.98 million camshafts in FY '24 as compared to 5.8 million in FY '23. And out of this number, the company machined 2.98 million camshafts in FY '24 compared to 3.1 million last year.

items.statement: Retrofit conversion time reduced to 8-10 hours per vehicle in India via process standardization and supply chain simplification.
items.quote: We are able to convert 1 vehicle or the retrofitting, we can use 8-10 hours.
