items.quote: At PCL, we manufacture brake components, so it's still automotive, but it's not engine-dependent, let's put it like that. We have ramped up the volume. Customer is already -- I mean, we're already shipping commercially to this customer for the last 2-3 months and we should see higher volumes in the coming year. Similarly, at MEMCO, we have an instrumentation customer, which we are growing with com

items.statement: EMOSS developing new modular powertrain platform for off-highway niche applications (waste trucks, sweepers, cranes) to launch in ~2 years.
items.quote: We're developing a platform which will be extremely modular, extremely flexible. We will be working with some of the largest suppliers in the world that will allow us to be extremely competitive on cost and provide some very unique solutions in the European kind of off-highway vehicle application which should start kicking in the next 2 years or so I would say.

items.statement: PCL serves 50+ global customers across 14 plants in 3 countries; 15+ products beyond automotive.
items.quote: The company now has 14 plants in three countries, serving over 50 marquee global customers and manufacturing over 15 different products catering to various industries, which are not restricted to the automotive industry only.

items.statement: EMOSS India deployed 25+ trial vehicles with 15+ key customers in logistics, e-commerce, waste management.
items.quote: We have already successfully deployed over 25 vehicles with 15-plus key customers in logistics, e-commerce, waste management, etcetera.

items.statement: EMOSS competitors are niche powertrain integrators of similar size in Europe/US and OEMs doing own truck electrification.
items.quote: They're all in the similar size as what we operate in, whether they're in Europe or the US. And mainly in these 2 geographies in a similar size that we operate in at this point of time, I would say. But they are again, niche powertrain manufacturers or integrators like us. And then the obvious competitors are the OEMs that do electrification of trucks themselves.

items.statement: Government discussions ongoing for financial incentives on LCV retrofitment; policy not yet declared; business model based on non-subsidized economics.
items.quote: Yes, I think there is discussion within the government and they're involved in certain forums regarding the financial incentives for retrofitment. However, it's not yet clear and the new policy, which is yet to be implemented by the government has to be declared.

items.statement: Retrofit business working capital needs can be met via debt at PCL level; no equity raise planned currently.
items.quote: Yes, I think, at this point, it can be done at PCL level quite comfortably with raising -- I mean, working capital can be bought in terms of debt, right? It doesn't need to have equity capital at this point.

items.statement: European subsidiaries operate as standalone P&L entities; no cash support from PCL India parent.
items.quote: None of the subsidiaries are taking any financial benefits from PCL from the stand-alone company. The companies operate on their own as stand-alone companies and are completely P&L at that level, which they take care of. So there is no cash that is being shelled out from the parent company to the subsidiaries.

items.statement: EMOSS Europe faces headwinds: recession, public spending slowdown, EV subsidy pushback, lackluster growth forecast.
items.quote: EMOSS is facing significant headwinds in Europe. This is due to the overall recessionary trends, a slowdown in public spending, pushback on EV subsidies and a general lackluster growth forecast.

items.statement: Retrofit scale-up dependent on customer demand; supply chain for battery packs/BMS could be bottleneck.
items.quote: The bottleneck can more be the supply chain and availability of components, battery packs, BMS, things like that.

We expect to sustain the EBITDA at the level which we have previously guided.

Probably, you can take a little bit of your view s, but we would like to convey these levels on a prudent basis.

items.quote: Furthermore, I would like to remind that the company has redeemed its tax free bonds amounting to INR100 crores in December 2023 and as of now, the company is practically debt -free, with only INR23 crores as long-term debt.

items.quote: In recognition of our financial performance, the Bo ard has recommended a final dividend of INR2.25 per share, aggregating to INR59.19 crores. Coupled with the interim dividends paid during the year, the total dividend for the financial year '23 -'24 amounts to INR256.50 crores, which is 32 percentage of the profit after tax.

items.quote: Shipbuilding, also August '24. It is actually that the crane is getting installed, we probably are putting a picture after this call. So, the crane is halfway through. items.quote: On a cash flow basis, we should be -- with most of the capex program being done, we do expect that we should generate free cash flow from financial year '25, and the cash profit should be close to about INR500 crores as far as our cash flow from operations is concerned, INR400 crores, INR500 crores.

items.quote: I think as far as the profit after tax is concerned, that should come positive from FY '26.

items.quote: So FY'25, it would be close to about 4 million to 5 million. So that would be close to about INR35-odd crores to INR40-odd crores, which in the last financial -- or financial year '24 stood at about INR100 crores.

items.quote: So yes, 15% -- 14% to 15% kind of growth in the CRAMS revenue should very much be doable.

items.quote: We're seeing an increase in the orders from the existing customers where the commercial supply are being supplied out or will be supplied out of Bavla. So that is number one. Number two, we have already seen new customers coming to the Bavla side.

items.statement: No major capex planned; free cash flow generation to reduce net debt over 2-3 years

items.statement: Q1-Q2 FY25 expected better than Q4 FY24; H2 FY25 much higher growth
items.quote: If we have to break it up quarter-wise, it is not ideal for our kind of business, but Q1, Q2 should be good quarters than what we have seen in Q4 FY '25 but we will see the second half of the year posting on much, much higher growth than what we've seen in the first half.

items.statement: Revenue expected to grow at least 15% annually for next 3 years

items.statement: Rate growth in FY25 should not be less than FY24

items.statement: Q1 FY25 will be much better than Q1 FY24 for owned company

items.quote: We expect our operational inventory to be about 120 + hotels with over 11,000 rooms by end of FY25.

items.statement: Pipeline addition of 2,000-3,000 rooms in FY25; openings of 1,200-2,000 rooms
items.quote: I do not think this is guidance when I say that we are very confident that we have 2,000-3,000 more rooms on our pipeline this year. And our endeavour is very simple, I can say it will be between from 1,200 - 2,000.

items.statement: Debt reduction to start in FY25; net debt zero within 4 years at latest
items.quote: So, debt reduction will start from this year. And there are 2 views, as I have said earlier. We are very confident that our debt will be 0 within the next 4 years, we will be net debt 0

items.statement: Renovation spend of Rs. 100 crore each in FY25 and FY26; ~65% opex, ~35% capex

items.statement: Keys portfolio target EBITDA of Rs. 60 crore per year minimum by October 2025
items.quote: Our target EBITDA for Keys would be Rs. 60 crore a year, minimum. And I think we will be getting there certainly by next October.

items.statement: Renovation impact on EBITDA margin was ~1.4% in Q4 FY24 (2% of revenue vs 0.6% prior year)
items.quote: It's about a 1.4% impact on overall EBITDA.

items.quote: I do not see any demand spilling over from Q1 to Q2. I think that there was a slowdown in demand in May partly due to weather, partly due to elections, and that is galloping back actually in June.

items.statement: IT hiring slowdown impacting Bangalore/Hyderabad occupancy; recovery expected from Q3 FY25

items.statement: FY24 total income INR82.41 crores, up 0.13% YoY; EBITDA INR14.75 crores, up 43% YoY; PAT INR5.89 crores, up 22.77% YoY

items.statement: Election cycles cause order delays every 5 years; international diversification aims to mitigate this dependency

So with all this, everything, it could be around INR12 crore

items.quote: the Bangalore facility itself will be about 70,000 square fest. So for us to get that plant also fully oceupied will take about 2 years, 2,5 years with such a large facility

items.statement: Raw material (steel) pricing environment benign; large new steel capacities coming online in next six months expected to keep prices stable.
items.quote: Raw material scenario seems to be very benign. I think I do not expect any problems as far as steel pricing is concerned. Lot of large steel capacities arc coming on stream in next six months. So, that should be okay

items.quote: We have changed our entire strategy of sales and got away from more higher volume sales. Even within the earth moving industry, there are lots of components which are high in volume and sales value, but the value addition is lower. So now we have tried to move away from that.

items.statement: Laser cutting capacity in India grown ~500% in 2 years, but fabrication entry barriers remain high; large OEMs reducing vendor bases, limiting new entrant threat.

items.statement: Company was debt-free in Sep 2023; has since taken small loans for capex; FY25 growth to be funded primarily from internal accruals with some debt; equity infusion only if large opportunity arises.
items.quote: Actually, last year in September we had become debt-free and then after that we have taken some small loans because of capex requirements. So going forward also at least in the coming year a good part of growth whatever we have planned will be out of internal aceruals. There will be some loan requirements also

items.statement: Investing in training facility in Gujarat and automation (robotics) to contain manpower costs; target to increase sales 50-60% without adding headcount.
items.quote: And we want to go for increased automation with robotics and other simple special pupose machines or assisting machines, ctestera. So the idea is to keep manpower numbers at the same level and increase sales from here by 50% or 60% from where we are and not add any people

items.statement: Domestic growth challenged by difficulty adding new large OEM customers who are limiting vendor bases; export focus increased to offset this.
items.quote: I'n not finding that we are definitely struggling to add customers to our profile. So, we can grow at that pace. If we want to grow at 20% or 20% plus, then the only way to do that is o add customers to what we have. And that part is proving to be very difficult

items.statement: Revenue potential from current and new facilities estimated at INR 250-300 crore with balanced equipment and manpower.
items.quote: So with this, new facility in place and all the existing setup, actually, with balancing cquipment and people and all that, it can be scaled up very substantially from here in the sense of, INR250 crores, INR300 crores business the whole company can do with this kind of facility

items.statement: Export revenue potential could equal or exceed domestic business in coming years; currently at very low base (INR 2-5 crore).
items.quote: In the coming years, if this what trends I see exports could grow so much that it could be as big or even bigger than the domestic business. That's the kind of potential which I see in the exports business.

items.statement: Management will not provide forward guidance on growth or margins
items.quote: No, we will not be doing any forward guidance.

items.statement: Global outbound travel expected to fully recover by end of 2024 and reach $2.7 trillion by 2027
items.quote: Post COVID, revival in outbound travel has been strong and full recovery is expected by the end of this year. Historically, outbound travel has grown at a pace of 5-6% every year. So, global travel spend is expected to reach nearly US $2.7 trillion by the year 2027.

items.statement: India outbound travel spending surged 24% to $17 billion in FY24 with 8-11% projected air passenger growth
items.quote: Overseas travel spending has surged to US $17 billion in this last financial year, marking a notable 24% increase over the previous year. Projections indicate an anticipated growth in international air passenger traffic by 8% to 11%.

items.statement: Monthly transacting buyers outside India grew 20% driving 31% international GTV growth; enterprise buyers grew 8% driving 19% overall GTV growth
items.quote: Our monthly transacting buyers outside of India grew by around 20%, which led to a growth of 31% in GTV in our international business. At an enterprise level, our monthly transacting buyer base grew by 8%, which led to an overall increase in GTV by 19%.

items.statement: Air take rate steady state at 2.5%; air gross profit expected between 1.2-1.5%
items.quote: So, considering the current situation, we believe that 2.5% should be a steady state growth or the take rate number for air business and similarly, for the gross profit numbers, we expect to maintain it between 1.5% to 1.2%.

items.statement: Significant investment planned in technology and data teams; costs will increase going forward
items.quote: No. I think there is no cost optimization possible, Pratyush, and tech resources remain expensive. So, our significant investment will continue to go into building out the technology and data teams. From the perspective of how we should look at this going forward, we do intend to increase the number of people in the tech team. So, you will see some increase in costs on those heads going forward.

items.statement: 26,500 monthly transacting buyers total with 18,500 in India; international buyers grew 20% vs 8% enterprise growth due to India base effect
items.quote: In fact, in 2024, out of roughly 26,500 buyers, 18,500 are sitting in India. So, while that number has grown, that number is growing at a slow percentage because of the base effect. So, hence the enterprise growth number looks lesser.

items.statement: 85-90% of international business naturally hedged in USD/GBP/EUR; India hotel payments hedged via forwards; airline payments in INR
items.quote: In our international business, a majority of our business is naturally hedged because we are selling in so many countries and buying from so many countries from different suppliers. So let us say, for example, selling in USD and also collecting in USD and making payment to suppliers in USD. So, around 85%-90% of my business in currencies like USD, GBP and Europe in naturally hedged.

items.statement: Working capital remains negative; trade receivables and payables increased due to Jumbonline consolidation and hotel mix with longer booking window
items.quote: Notably, our working capital continues to remain negative. As of March end 2024, there has been a substantial increase in trade receivables and trade payables amount as compared to the past year. This has been primarily due to consolidation of financial numbers of our new acquisition Jumbonline as well as due to the increase in the overall mix of hotel business.

items.statement: IPO raised INR 1,550 Cr total with INR 400 Cr primary infusion for future growth goals
items.quote: The total size of the IPO was INR 1,550 Crore, with INR 400 Crore being the primary infusion of capital. This capital injection will enable us to fulfill our funding requirements to achieve our future goals.

items.statement: Completed 4 acquisitions in 5 years including Jumbonline for Southern European beach hotels; acquisition thesis focuses on adding buyer base or supply base globally
items.quote: Over the last 5 years, we have completed 4 acquisitions, enhancing our global reach and market position. Most recently, we had acquired Jumbonline, which is an aggregator of Southern European Beach Hotel supply. We will continue to look for more opportunities for inorganic growth.

items.statement: Jumbonline contributed INR 36 Cr revenue and INR 3.5 Cr PAT in FY24; material impact expected in coming year
items.quote: So, Swapnil, there was only INR 36 Crore of revenue that was contributed by Jumbo in the last FY numbers. So, we will see some material impact in the Jumbonline in the coming year, but it was not very material for last year. In terms of PAT, the contribution was about INR 3.5 Crore from the Jumbonline business.

items.statement: SG&A at 2.5% of GTV with 0.5% variable (hosting, payment gateway) and 2% fixed; operating leverage expected long-term
items.quote: So, the SG&A cost is at around 2.5%. Two components in the SG&A cost, which is hosting and bandwidth as well as the payment gateway cost, which is prima facie semi-variable or variable in nature basically, which will grow in line most probably with the growth of GTV or the revenue. items.statement: UAE corporate tax of 9% effective current financial year will increase overall effective tax rate

So, our overall effective tax rate would increase from what currently we are having.

items.statement: Travel volatility from macroeconomic and political events is fundamental risk; global diversification provides some hedge
items.quote: Travel is highly volatile. It doesn't take long for travel to be doing well and then some global macro event to happen and disrupt travel. So, that is definitely a risk. We are also exposed to a very global travel industry. So the chances of something going wrong in some part of the world is always there, though it also adds a hedge for us because we are not overly concentrated in a certain market

items.statement: Gross profit as percentage of GTV improved to 3.47% from 3.28%; EBITDA grows faster than gross profit due to operating leverage
items.quote: Gross profit as a percentage of GTV for the full year improved to 3.47% from 3.28% last year. EBITDA grows faster than gross profit because of operating leverage, which is quite well demonstrated this year.

items.statement: Hotels provide differentiated pricing for B2B channel vs OTAs as travel agents package rates with flights and ancillaries
items.quote: Hotels usually provide differentiated pricing for the online channels like OTA and B2B channel like ours because our channels serve different kind of traveler. items.quote: We structure Europe into three different distinct regions because it is so large and important for us and we have three different regional leaders running Europe, in different parts of Europe is a testament to the fact that we have very high hopes from this market. items.statement: Phase II capex of ~₹500 crore covering denim, non-denim, yarn, and air-jet weaving expansion
items.quote: So, basically, so expansion that we're talking about, expansion is coming in denim, that'll enhance the capacity from 1.8 crores to 2.52 crores. It is coming in, basically, it is coming in non-denim of 1.8 crores.

items.quote: Our expansion will lead to increase of capacity of around 72 lakh metres from 1.8 crore metre per annum to 2.52 crore per annum. Expansion in non-denim, so we are entering non-denim segment also right now, which will lead to enhancement of capacity from 0 to 1.8 crore metres per annum.

And along with the developments we have an estimated order book of 35 lakh metres right now with the clients like Marks & Spencer, H&M, and numerous clients like this along with the domestic clients.

items.statement: New brand tie-ups with Reliance and ZARA; 90% repeat order rate; 0% rejection rate since inception
items.quote: We have started working with all these brands recently, and we've tied up with Reliance and ZARA. And these are the few players that we've tied up with and which we can disclose right now. And these are all new players.

items.statement: Yarn booked on order date to pass through raw material cost; best-in-class cotton buying claimed
items.quote: when we sell the fabric to a customer, we take the current rate of the yarn. We book the yarn on the current date, and then we sell the fabric. So we mitigate th e variation of raw material there

items.quote: In textile industry, there is no long-term tie up like this. That you have a written tie up of 10 lakh metres per month. There's no long-term tie up in textile industries. It is a job work then. So it all depends on the price variations and all the developments that we're doing.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target of Rs 650-700 crore
items.quote: So the revenue of ₹650 crores to 700 crores.

items.statement: Conservative PAT margin target of 6.5% post expansion

items.statement: Total project investment around Rs 300 crore including working capital

items.quote: Peak debt number will be around ₹220 crores of term loan.

items.statement: Weaving denim and non-denim expansion completed this month; spinning by October 2024
items.quote: Spinning division, yes. For, weaving, for denim and for non-denim, it will be completed this month itself.

items.quote: if I talk about 1.8 crores, we have existing capacity of 1.8 crores that is already running at 100% capacity. That can generate the revenue of 350 to 380 crores.

items.quote: The additional capacity, if I talk about of 72 lakhs plus 1.8 lakhs, 1.8 crores has a maximum capacity of around 550 crores, the fabric division that I'm talking about.

items.quote: So I'm targeting with this we will be able to achieve roughly 60% to 70% production in this year.

items.statement: Current order book 35 lakh metres, up from 17-20 lakh metres a year ago
items.quote: I think we have an order book of like 35 lakh metres. If I talk about last year at the same time, what would be your order book approximate? Nasir Khan: That time my order book was around 17 lakhs to 20

items.quote: Currently, we have an order book of export of 5 lakh metres right now. We have about 5 lakh to 6 lakh metres of exports orders in hand. Now, let's assume that we will have an order book of around 15 lakhs to 17 lakhs of trading.

items.statement: Tied up with Reliance Trends; order book covers two months supply
items.quote: We have tied up with Reliance Trends, which have a very huge brands portfolio right now. items.statement: Target to reduce trader segment by 25%; aim for 25-30% brands, 25-30% exports, 20-25% cutters
items.quote: So we are targeting to reduce the trading segment by 25%. So we'll keep a portfolio of around 20%, 25% of cutters, 25% to 30% of brands, and 25%, 30% of exports, and the rest will be divided into trading.

items.statement: H2 FY24 EBITDA margin 13.5% considered sustainable
items.quote: It is very sustainable for us. Basically I will tell you that when you visit the plant, and the kind of booking you see with us, because defining something in the books is a different thing.

items.statement: EBITDA margin FY24 was 12.43%
items.quote: We did have, it was around, I think the EBITDA margin was 12.43%, I guess.

items.statement: Utility cost reduction example: from Rs 30 to Rs 24 per unit due to shared utilities
items.quote: if I talk about costing is ₹30 right now, then our costing will be reduced ₹24. I'm giving you examples, the utility costing I'm talking about because we have installed the plant in the same utility.

items.statement: Power rate incentives in Rajasthan and MP to save Rs 5.5-6 crore annually at full capacity (1.5 lakh units/day)
items.quote: the power rate that has been offered to us. I'll personally share it with you, but that itself makes a huge difference, because we'll have a consumption of around 1,50,000 units per day after starting of all the plants. And that will impact, that will give us a return of estimatedly , it will make an impact on our balance sheet of minimum 5.5 Cr to 6 Cr, if I compare to the existing units.

items.statement: Job work outsourcing of Rs 18-19 crore last year to be cut by 50% with in-house weaving
items.quote: last year we paid an hour. We did a job work of around 18 to 19 crores of job work we did outside. So that particular job work will be minimised to, I think 50% because the capacity will also increase of us.

items.statement: Total subsidies (capital, interest, power, land) estimated Rs 130-150 crore over 7 years
items.quote: My subsidy will exceed from ₹130 crores to ₹150 crores including interest subsidies, electricity subsidies, capital subsidies that will be directly credited to the account.

items.statement: First subsidy tranche of Rs 10-15 crore expected next quarter
items.quote: I hope that in the next quarter, the initial first tranche of ₹10 - ₹15 crores will be released.

items.statement: Capital subsidy 30% of plant & machinery + building investment, released over 7 years
items.quote: the total investment in plant, machinery and building will be subsidised by 30%. The actual subsidiary that will be released will be around 32%, 33%. But on the conservative side, I'm talking about 30% right now.

items.statement: Interest subsidy 7% on term loan, released quarterly after drawdown schedule
items.quote: Interest side, if I talk about so, basically if I say ₹200 crores of loan is my loan, then you can calculate 7% on ₹200 crores. After preparing a drawdown schedule, you can, the repayment will be reduced and the remaining 7% subsidy will be released on quarterly basis.

items.statement: Receivable days currently around 60 days
items.quote: The receivable days right now, it has increased a little bit, but the average is around 60 days.

items.statement: Working capital limit Rs 80 crore sanctioned with 25% margin; comfortable for FY25 needs
items.quote: we have a working capital of ₹80 crores that was sanctioned by the bank along with 25% margin of ours. Chirag Jain: So we would be competing on that. Nasir Khan: Yes, 110 to 120. That is, I guess, we can work with that right

items.statement: Non-denim revenue target Rs 250-300 crore; balance denim for FY25
items.quote: if I talk about non-denim, non-denim will have a revenue segment of around ₹250 crores to ₹300 crores and the rest part will be denim.

items.statement: Implemented SAP S/4 HANA Cloud public version in textile composite mill
items.quote: we are the first company in India to implement SAP, SAP S/4 HANA Cloud version, public cloud version in a textile composite mill.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility and government stability cited as key risks; subsidies not factored into margin guidance
items.quote: raw material prices, we have an extreme fluctuations happening. Right now the government had become a little unstable, but it is stable, i.e. the same government will continue, so, we don't have problems in the government issues also.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth expected to be very close to double-digit
items.quote: Maybe very close to double-digit.

items.statement: Target 30-35% of business from high-margin products in next 3-4 years
items.quote: In the next 3-4 years, we target nearly 30%-35% business will be derived from high margin products.

items.statement: High-margin non-acid chloride products could lift overall EBITDA to 22-23% when they reach 30-35% of volume
items.quote: Once we are able to commercialize these products, 30%-35% of our volume should be probably EBITDA of about 22%-23%.

items.statement: New non-acid chloride products carry 15-20% higher EBITDA margin than current portfolio
items.quote: This can be almost, you can say, 15% to 20% higher than what we are earning today. In terms of the EBITDA margin, you can say.

items.statement: New acid chloride products in US and Korea have 1,000-4,000 MT/year potential each but traction will take time
items.quote: When I say good potentials these are like; 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000 metric ton a year kind of potentials. But it is going to take some time before we really, really see some major traction out of this.

items.statement: Non-acid chloride pipeline potential INR 200-250 crore when fully commercialized
items.quote: Potential of these products is quite good. It can go to INR200 crores to INR250 crores when you put all these products together.

items.statement: Greenfield capex not high on consideration; evaluating brownfield, job-work or small facility takeover with lower investment
items.quote: Probably a facility which has some possibility to just modify and then start production. Those kinds of options we are looking at. So, with little limited or lower investment, we can take less risk.

items.statement: Vizag greenfield project withdrawn due to customer growth plans halting post-COVID; no structural change in business
items.quote: Their growth plans have also kind of halted. And whatever business we had at that time or whatever business we have at this point in time, as I mentioned, there is no structural change.

items.statement: FY24 capacity utilisation 68%; targeting 78-79% in FY25
items.quote: 68% has been FY'24 and about 78%-79% we are expecting for FY'25.

items.statement: Peak revenue at full utilisation and normal pricing around INR 900-920 crore
items.quote: If we are able to utilize everything well and at whatever is the normal price that we can fetch, we can reach around INR900 crores-INR920 crores.

items.statement: Polymer volumes fell ~25% in FY24 due to customer de-stocking and cautious ordering; no structural demand loss
items.quote: Overall requirement from the customers reduced because of their end product demand being subdued, of course, on a temporary basis. As I mentioned, structure of the business has not changed.

items.statement: Aramid fibre demand growing steadily; Far East players expanding capacity, some doubling
items.quote: Some of the companies in Far East market like Korea and Japan, they are expanding their capacity for aramid fibres. Some are in fact almost doubling their capacity.

items.statement: FY24 revenue decline driven by both volume drop and price reduction as raw material costs fell 30-35% from FY23 peaks
items.quote: A couple of our raw material prices went down by almost 30%-35% than what it was in FY23.

items.statement: New products contributed ~INR 25-30 crore in FY24; 5-6 acid chlorides introduced over 3-4 years
items.quote: So, there has been contribution of about INR25 crores, INR30 crores coming from some of these new products.

items.statement: Customers ordering conservatively with back-to-back orders; no long-term contracts currently; dialogue ongoing for stable supply agreements
items.quote: Nobody is very keen to enter into something which will commit themselves for a very long time. They are just waiting and watching to see how this uncertain situation unfolds.

items.statement: Over 85% revenue from exports; freight costs rose in H2 FY24 due to Red Sea crisis but largely passed to customers
items.quote: With over 85% of our total business coming from the export market, freight and logistic costs have increased to some extent in second half due to Red Sea crisis. However, a large part of our freight cost is paid by customers.

items.statement: NSE listing application nearly ready; advisors reviewing documentation from 1970s-80s; will apply shortly
items.quote: Our advisors are examining this information and data in detail and once it is done, we will be applying to NSE very shortly.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 14 per share (140%) for FY24
items.quote: Board has recommended a dividend of INR14, which is 140% per equity share of this value of INR10/- for the financial year 2024.

items.statement: Buyback suggestion will be placed before board; decision will balance investment needs and shareholder returns
items.quote: We will definitely put it to the board. But on one hand, you are asking me about when you are going to invest in new facilities and on the other hand, you are asking, telling me to do buyback. So, we'll have to see what is right for business.

items.statement: Silox India investment is illiquid (book value INR 309 crore, cost INR 3 crore); receiving good dividends but encashment difficult
items.quote: Valuation as per the balance sheet of that company is INR309 crores. Now, as I mentioned, that is just valuation. This is not money that we have invested. What we had invested was only INR3 crores.

items.statement: Fixed asset increase of ~45% driven by Ind AS right-of-use assets (ISO tank leases ~INR 70 crore) and Thionyl Chloride capacity modification (~INR 32 crore)
items.quote: Right of use assets, for example, has grown almost by how many crores? INR70 crores, right? INR70 crores. Now when I say INR70 crores, it is not actually the asset increase. It is purely the way accounting is done.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR500 crores expected by 2027 with EBITDA margins of 22%-24%
items.quote: we are on the way and we are hopeful that with the Ethiopia orders coming in and the new facility going upstream in 2025, we expect to achieve the same by 2027

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth targeted at 25%-30% year-on-year with export mix 60%-65% and domestic 30%-40%
items.quote: what we understand is the growth will be around 25 %-30% on year-on-year. And we'll be maintaining almost the same ratio of 60 %-65% for exports and 30 %-40% for local market, domestic

items.statement: EBITDA margin outlook for FY25 maintained or improved at 18%-22%
items.quote: we'll be almost maintaining or improving the EBITDA margin of 18% -22% around -- between 18%-22%

items.statement: Khopoli greenfield project capex ~INR100 crores; first floor slab completion targeted this month, validation planned May 2025
items.quote: Right now, this month we'll be completing the first floor slab and we foresee that May 25 is we'll start with the validation

items.statement: Ethiopia facility capex of INR50 crores incurred till 2021; no major capex since production start

items.statement: Final dividend of INR1 per share (100% of face value) declared for FY24
items.quote: The company has also declared a final dividend of INR1 per share i.e. 100% per equity share having face value of INR1 each for the financial year 2023-24 as a final dividend.

items.statement: US FDA approval for 6 colors; ISO 9001:2000, GFSI compliant; Korean, Iranian, Thai FDA approvals also held
items.quote: we already have approvals from U.S. FDA. And in addition to this, we follow various quality systems like ISO 9001 : 22000. We are GFSI compliant. So, that's to show we have approvals from other various FDAs like the Korean, Iranian. So, even the individual Thai FDA.

items.statement: R&D team includes PhDs and qualified chemists; R&D expense 4-5% of sales (~INR12 cr in FY24)
items.quote: Our R&D expense would come to around 4% -5% of our sales.

items.statement: PAT declined due to steel price volatility; steel prices fell from Rs 80/kg in March 2023 to Rs 57/kg in March 2024, reducing revenue despite higher tonnage.
items.quote: Due to volatility in prices of Steel. In March, 2023 prices of steel were around Rs.80/- whereas in March, 2024 prices of steel showed a decline to Rs. 57/-, due to such downward trend for the whole financial year the revenue of the company has declined inspite of increase in production capacity/tonnage.

items.statement: Quarterly revenue and tonnage: Q1 Rs 28 Cr/787t, Q2 Rs 26 Cr/501t, Q3 Rs 25 Cr/980t, Q4 Rs 24 Cr/1100t.
items.quote: In Q1: Revenue was 28 Crs., tonnage was 787 ton. In Q2: Revenue was 26 Crs., tonnage was 501 ton. In Q3: Revenue was 25 Crs., tonnage was 980 ton. In Q4: Revenue was 24 Crs., tonnage was 1100 ton.

items.statement: Management targets operating profit margin to increase by 1% in the current fiscal year.
items.quote: The management will try that the Operating Profit Margin increases from 1% this year.

items.statement: PEB order book covers next 2.5-3 months; plant booked for execution till October 2024.
items.quote: For Pre-Engineering Buildings we have order book for next 2.5-3 months and for execution the plant is booked till October,2024.

items.statement: Unit II current capacity 800 tonnes/month; target 2000 tonnes/month in 3-4 years after installing more machines and hiring staff.
items.quote: In Unit I, the production capacity of 300 tonnes for Roofing Sheets and approx 100 tonnes of Pre-Engineering Buildings, whereas, in Unit II, the production capacity as on date is 800 tonnes per month and in future the same can be increased to 2000 tonnes.

items.statement: Future capex will be funded from internal accruals, not from shareholders.
items.quote: There may be capital expenditure in coming future, but the same will be from our own accurals and not from the side of shareholders.

items.statement: After full phase completion and machine installation, turnover can reach Rs 200-250 Cr in future.
items.quote: Therefore, in Unit II after completion of all the phases and instalment of more machines, the turnover can reach to Rs. 200-250 Crs. in future.

items.statement: Revenue is directly proportional to steel prices.
items.quote: Yes, steel prices are directly proportional to the revenue.

items.statement: Built accommodation for ~80 labourers, started canteen services, and forming MOUs with ITIs and skill centres for fitters, welders, grinders.
items.quote: Sir, to solve this issue we have taken following measures: 1. The accommodation facilities for approx. 80 labours has been arranged by constructing 16-18 houses. 2. Canteen Services has been started, so that labours do not starve for food. 3. We have approached many Industrial Training Institutes and Skill Development Centres to form strong team of fitter, welder, grinder men as per our requiremen

items.statement: Total debt repaid in FY24 was around Rs 2.13 Cr.
items.quote: Total debt repaid in FY 23-24 was around Rs.2,12,66,000/-

items.statement: FY24 PAT margin 3.36%, operating profit margin before tax 6.29%, operating profit Rs 6.66 Cr.
items.quote: PAT margin in FY 23-24 3.36% Operating Profit Margin before Tax in FY 23- 24 6.29% Operating profit in value was Rs. 6,65,86,000/-

items.statement: Unit I (36,000 sq ft) rented out at ~Rs 3.15 lakh/month; Unit II expanded to 300,000 sq ft in phases.
items.quote: Unit I is non -operative and it will be given on monthly -rent for Rs. 3.15 Lakhs approx..

items.statement: Suven entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a controlling 51% stake in Sapala Organics, a Hyderabad-based CDMO specializing in oligonucleotide drugs and nucleic acid building blocks.
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that Suven has entered into a Definitive Agreement for the Acquisition of a Controlling Stake in Sapala Organics.

items.statement: Initial consideration is Rs 2,295 million for 51% stake on a fully diluted basis; 100% acquisition expected at 13x-15x EBITDA multiple over the next three years, financed through cash reserves.
items.quote: Subject to the customary adjustments for net cash and working capital, the initial consideration is Rs. 2,295 million for an acquisition of 51% stake on a fully diluted basis. We expect the 100% acquisition to be valued at 13x to 15x times EBITDA multiple, contingent on the financial performance, primarily EBITDA, over the next three years.

items.statement: Transaction expected to be EPS-accretive from the first year of acquisition and will not affect the current merger scheme with Cohance.
items.quote: The transaction is expected to be EPS-accretive from the first year of acquisition and we do not expect this acquisition to affect the current merger scheme with Cohance.

items.statement: Sapala's business expected to match or exceed the market growth rate of 20%+ CAGR in the mid-to-long term due to a smaller base.
items.quote: In a mid-term-to-long-term. It will match or exceed the current market growth. That's the internal view that we have, because the base is lower and smaller.

items.statement: Sapala FY24 revenues over Rs 670 million with adjusted EBITDA margins at 45%+; adjusted revenue growing at 18% CAGR over the last three years.
items.quote: In FY'24 Sapala's revenues were over Rs. 670 million and the adjusted EBITDA margins being at 45%-plus. As shared in the investor deck, the adjusted revenue has been growing at a CAGR of 18% for the last three years.

items.statement: Plans to create a GMP manufacturing facility at one of Suven's expanded platform sites to support future growth as molecules progress from preclinical to commercial stages.
items.quote: And one of the important elements as a part of the deal is, we end up supporting the growth of the organization by creating a GMP manufacturing facility. Hence, we don't have any capacity constraint right now, and as it is a predominantly R&D, we have enough capacities; however, in view of the future growth, we have plans to create a GMP manufacturing site in one of our expanded platform sites.

items.statement: Current operations are predominantly R&D-led with kilolitre-scale capacity for basic amidites; no capacity constraints currently, but GMP facilities planned for future clinical and commercial scale-up.
items.quote: This is predominantly R&D-led activity and today, the basic amidites or some of the compounds that we do manufacturing are in kilolitres capacity. Otherwise, from a capacity standpoint, it is predominantly on R&D side of it; however, when the molecule grows into the clinical phase from preclinical into commercial, what we need is GMP facilities.

items.statement: Sapala has a diversified innovator customer base across US (40%), Europe (30%), and Japan (20%), including big biopharma and oligo-focused CDMO players; top five customers contribute less than 50% of revenue.
items.quote: Today, Sapala has innovator customer base across US, Europe and Japan. Broad geography, average sale split, the last few years between US, Europe and Japan is around 40, 30 and 20, which also means is a good mix of big biofirms, which includes oligo-focused CDMO players and that's how the current business mix is around the companies.

items.statement: Customer addition is happening regularly, along with addition of molecules for existing customers and product progress; Suven's existing relationships with top innovator companies expected to accelerate this.
items.quote: Yes. Addition of the customers is happening, on top of it addition of molecules for the same line of customers is also happening. Finally, product progress is actually seen and Sapala is along with the product progress as well.

items.statement: Sapala specializes in locked and bridged nucleic acids, tricyclo DNA, and GalNAC compounds, positioning it as one of few global players capable of delivering such specialized oligonucleotide solutions.
items.quote: Sapala capabilities in locked and bridged nucleic acid, Tricyclo DNA, GalNAC positions it as one of the few players globally capable of delivering such specialized solution, which the market is looking for.

items.statement: Competitive landscape is unique with no directly comparable peers; some companies are closely related but not exactly comparable due to Sapala's unique combination of competencies under one roof.
items.quote: As you understand, there is a very unique combination of having bridged nucleotides and galvanic compounds and tricyclic compounds. So, it's very hard to decide; however, there are some companies who are closely related, but not exactly comparable.

items.statement: Synergies from combining Sapala's R&D depth with Suven's customer access and manufacturing capabilities expected to materialize within two to four years, depending on clinical success of pipeline.
items.quote: But, as you understand, our success is depending on the clinical success of a pipeline, which means anywhere visible case studies can be built with synergies at least within two to four years' timeframe is what we see so which comes back to the same time period or which can be a little early also.

items.statement: Dr. P. Yella Reddy, Sapala's promoter and CEO with 20+ years experience in Japan, will continue as CEO for the next few years and serve as strategic advisor for Japan market entry across Suven and Cohance platforms.
items.quote: We plan to operate this business collaboratively with the current promoter, working as the CEO of Sapala Organics for the next few years as well as the strategic advisor for Japan region before we fully acquire 100% of Sapala.

items.statement: Acquisition structured with initial 51% stake purchase, balance 49% to be acquired over three to four years at 13x-15x EBITDA multiple based on future financial performance, ensuring alignment of interests.
items.quote: We're expecting to acquire 100% in a period of three to four years which again would be valued at 13 to 15 EBITDA multiple in the next three to four years.

items.statement: Gross written premium crossed INR 9,000 crores in FY24 with market share of 3.1% on GWP basis
items.quote: we have completed and crossed INR 9,000 crores of premium income in the last whole year. Overall market share on GWP basis is about 3.1.

items.statement: Net earned premium doubled from FY22 to FY24 reaching INR 7,000 crores
items.quote: if you look at the next line, which is the premium retention ratio, the premium retention ratio has also been increasing each year. And in FY '24, this number was about 85.8%.

items.statement: Combined ratio for FY24 was 108.7%, about 1% higher than previous year due to large property and NAT CAT losses
items.quote: Our combined ratio in FY '24 was 108.7, which is about 1% higher than the previous year. Most of it is related to some large losses in property, which we had and some NAT CAT losses.

items.statement: Profit after tax for FY24 was INR 182 crores, Q4 FY24 profit was INR 53 crores (double Q4 FY23)
items.quote: Our profit for the year is about INR 182 crores. And for the quarter, it's INR53 crores, which is double to what we had in quarter 4 of '23.

items.statement: Premium retention ratio increased to 85.8% in FY24, among highest in industry
items.quote: And in FY '24, this number was about 85.8%, which I believe would be amongst the highest in the industry.

items.statement: Own damage mix increased from 16% to 22%, TP reduced from 46% to 39%, health travel increased from 13% to 19% in FY24
items.quote: you can actually see our own damage mix has increased from 16% to 22% in FY '24. TP has actually reduced from 46% to 39%. Health travel NP has increased from 13% to 19%.

items.statement: Outgrew industry in motor OD (42% vs 17%), fire (19% vs 7%), health; de-grew motor TP by 11% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: industry has grown in motor own damage by about 17% against our 42%. TP is about 10%, which is similar to ours. Fire, industry grew by 7%, we grew by 19%. And health, etcetera, also, we grew more than the industry.

items.statement: Took corrective action in motor TP due to third-party inflation and minimum wage increases; de-grew TP by 11% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: we as a company always plan continuously look at businesses where we feel it doesn't make sense economically for us to do business. And we would actually then get out of those segments if we don't find the margins to be attractive.

items.statement: Own damage loss ratio improved year by year: 74%, 69%, 66%; TP loss ratio viewed over 3-4 year period
items.quote: if you look at our own damage loss ratios has been coming down year by year, 74, 69, 66. TP loss ratio has been coming down. But in TP loss ratio, we always look at loss ratio over a period of three years or four years

items.statement: Health loss ratio increased due to growth in employer-employee health business and lower data quality initially
items.quote: The loss ratio still was at about 72% lower than, I would say, the industry health loss ratio. And this has increased last year due to the growth in the employer -employee health insurance business.

items.statement: Property and engineering NAT CAT losses of INR 70 crores impacted combined ratio by only 1% due to high net earned premium base
items.quote: We actually had an impact of about INR70 crores, which basically meant that in case of property and engineering, this had a very, very significant impact. But what is interesting is that because we have a very high net earn ed premium of almost INR7,000 crores, the impact on the overall loss ratio for the year is only 1%.

items.statement: API integrations doubled in two years; 51% of policies now issued through APIs
items.quote: you can also see in two years, we have almost doubled the number of APIs we have. And now 51% of our policies are issued through the APIs.

items.statement: Assets under management grew organically by INR 2,700-2,800 crores in FY24; raised INR 350 crores sub-debt for solvency
items.quote: if you look at from FY23 to FY24, we have roughly increased organically the AUM by about INR2,700, INR2,800 crores. And this year we had raised INR 350 crores of sub-debt to support the solvency.

items.statement: Investment income crossed INR 1,000 crores, more than doubled from FY22; investment yield improved to 7.3% (up ~100 bps)
items.quote: The investment income is decent. We crossed INR1,000 crores in investment income. So if you actually see FY22 to FY24, our investment income has actually more than doubled. And you can also see that the investment yield is also now about 7.3%, which is almost 100 basis points better than the previous year.

items.statement: Equity allocation kept low at 1.6% due to solvency sensitivity; will increase equity allocation post IPO capital infusion
items.quote: Our equity allocation has continued to be lower. It's only 1.6%. And when we look at our solvency of 161%, since solvency ratio was a bit lower, any unrealized losses in equity passed through the solvency or passed through the P&L.

items.statement: Solvency ratio was 1.61 as of March 2024; expected to exceed 200% by June 2024 post IPO capital infusion of INR 1,125 crores
items.quote: our sense is this will be more than 200%. What exactly that number would be that we will know only on 30th of June, but we expect the solvency ratio to go beyond 200% definitely.

items.statement: Raised INR 1,125 crores through IPO; net worth increased by one-third; leverage will decrease this year then resume growth
items.quote: leverage obviously will go down this year because we have raised capital of about INR 1125 crores or so. So, our net worth will suddenly increase by one third. So, the leverage will go down.

items.statement: Reserving triangles show adequate reserving across whole account, motor TP, and non-TP lines; no negative surprises philosophy
items.quote: I think for us in Digit our philosophy, for reserving is that we need to always be adequately reserved. I think having surprises on reserving, negative surprises, is something which shouldn't really happen.

items.statement: IFRS 17 audited reconciliation published; IFRS profitability from year 3; regulator not yet mandating IFRS reporting format
items.quote: as of now the regulator is not asking us or any company to publish IFRS results. And in what shape and manner would the IFRS get implemented in India or by the regulator is something which we'll have to wait and see.

items.statement: Retail health insurance ~INR 60 crores; group health dominates portfolio; health business under industry stress due to portability and waiting period dynamics
items.quote: most of our portfolio would be gro up. And retail health insurance would be a smaller number. If I remember offhand, this would be close to about INR60 crores or so for last year

items.statement: Support motor TP de-tariffing; industry priority is TP rate increase (no increase in 4 years); free pricing would shift competition from commission to price
items.quote: our view is that sooner or later, one should have de -tariffing simply because this is the only segment where there is no free pricing. Secondly, when the pricing is fixed, then people play on the commission, on the acquisition cost.

items.statement: Channel agnostic strategy; broker channel includes OEM, corporate, retail, aggregators - all with different loss ratios and acquisition costs
items.quote: we as a company are channel agnostic which basically means that we try and steer business through all possible distribution channels, looking at their own each channels, own loss ratio as well as acquisition cost.

items.statement: No target channel or product mix; market dynamics change rapidly (e.g., OEM channel fluctuates with auto sales cycles)
items.quote: there is no real channel mix which we steer towards to say in 2 years this is the channel mix which we want. Because I think again, based on our understanding of business market changes very fast.

items.statement: B2B strategy (fire, engineering, group health) combines relationships, underwriting expertise, reinsurance capacity, and claims settlement ability; earned right to win daily
items.quote: it actually becomes a mix of all of this. As far as I think right to etc etera goes, as you rightly said, we are a small player in this. But despite that, we did INR800 crores of property premium last year.

items.statement: No guidance on combined ratio trajectory; business driven by profitability not growth targets; will de-grow unprofitable segments
items.quote: we don't really -- we are not really in a position to give any guidance and nor we want to give guidance because we don't drive our business from that perspective.

items.statement: NAT CAT losses unpredictable; expect 1/3 to 1/2 of FY24 losses annually but not uniformly distributed; impact limited by growing premium base
items.quote: One would expect, I would say, half of these losses or one third of these losses to come every year. But the losses will never, ever be uniformly distributed.

items.statement: Motor TP de-growth in Q4 FY24 driven by commercial vehicles (90% TP premium); will re-enter when market corrects
items.quote: if we de-gr ew in motor third -party, you can be sure that the de -growth would have happened more because of commercial vehicles, because commercial vehicles have almost 90% of the premium coming in from third-party.

items.statement: Acquisition of 100% of Penna Cement for INR 10,422 crore enterprise value, funded from internal accruals
items.quote: The transaction value, as you've already seen from our investor deck, is INR10,422 crores. It will be funded fully from our internal accruals.

items.statement: Adds 14 MTPA cement capacity (10 MTPA operational, 4 MTPA under construction) taking Adani Cement operational capacity to 89 MTPA
items.quote: It includes 14 million tons of cement capacity, of which 10 is operational, 4 is under construction. This will take Adani Cement's operational capacity to 89 million tons.

items.statement: INR 3,000 crore milestone payments for completing Krishnapatnam (2 MTPA) and Jodhpur (3 MTPA clinker) projects within 9-12 months
items.quote: So, in terms of the under -construction projects, we are going to release almost INR3,000 crores at different time intervals. This is the milestone to be achieved.

items.statement: Target 15% ROCE by FY27 at 80% capacity utilisation; operating capacity ~96 MTPA by end FY25 and ~110 MTPA by FY26
items.quote: we are targeting to achieve a ratio of almost 15%, and that we should start looking at from when we hit the capacity of, say, 80%, which we are targeting by, say, third year. So, one can safely assume that from '27, that is the return which we are looking at.

items.statement: 140 MTPA target by March 2028 on track; 20 MTPA already announced, 30 MTPA blueprint ready with land and mining in place
items.quote: So, we are well poised to hit our 140 million ton target, as we have been speaking in past.

items.statement: Expect INR 300/t cost efficiency from AFR, RE, cooler upgrades, logistics; INR 5-10/t pricing upside; total INR 500/t EBITDA kicker, reaching INR 1,500/t over 2 years
items.quote: I would say about INR300 per ton cost efficiency is something very doable. And on the pricing side as you know Ambuja ACC are A category price players. So there is always a INR5 to INR10 upside on the pricing.

items.statement: Will apply Ambuja/ACC brand playbook (base + 2 premium brands, OPC, blended) using Penna's multi-chamber silos; clinker quality supports full product range
items.quote: We have typically a base brand and we have two premium brands for each of the company which is the playbook we have for Pan India. In addition, for B2B segments, we have our power brands, OPC and also blended.

items.statement: AFR currently low at Penna; target 25-30% substitution like Ambuja/ACC; 1,000 MW solar/wind RE plan; behind-the-meter assets in Andhra
items.quote: On top we already have a great solar strategy. As you know AAA is in the process of putting 1000 megawatts of solar and wind. In Andhra, there is a lot of opportunity to put behind the meter assets as well.

items.statement: Re-entry into Sri Lanka via Penna's bulk terminal at Kankesanthurai; Adani Group building port there; coastal shipping strategy with 5 bulk terminals and 25,500t carrier
items.quote: Very interesting thing is it brings back Ambuja into Sri Lanka. You might be aware many years back Ambuja had a bulk cement terminal in Kale in Sri Lanka, which later became part of the Holcim.

items.statement: Two existing Penna plants have state incentives; Jodhpur plant eligible for better Rajasthan incentives; CCI approval expected to be smooth as share purchase
items.quote: They already have, in fact, and what we see is there is a good scope to further improve on that. But yes, two of their existing plants have it and then Rajasthan will have far better incentives to look forward to.

items.statement: Upfront equity ~INR 4,000 crore after INR 3,500 crore debt/liabilities; INR 10,000+ crore cash remaining post-acquisition by year-end
items.quote: After all of this also, by end of this year, my estimate is that we will be holding almost INR10,000 plus crores of cash.

items.statement: South India market share improves from 10% to ~20%; Pan-India share +2%; ACC undersupplied in South, Penna adds volume to serve demand
items.quote: This brings us to almost 20%. Importantly, apart from all the points Ajayji has highlighted, it gives me an opportunity of earning a ROCE of almost 15%.

items.statement: Top 5 players' South capacity share rises from 45% to ~55% post Penna + Kesoram consolidation; industry maturing
items.quote: while we know Ambuja Cements June 14, 2024 that Kesoram is getting consolidated with Ultra Tech and now Penna with us and so this will actually improve the share of the top five players to almost say 55

items.statement: Seller responsible for pending land acquisition for Jodhpur railway line and limestone reserves; indemnification for past litigations; milestone payments protect against delays
items.quote: whatever is the pending parcels of land which will be required for the railway line and for the limestone reserves in due course, they are acquiring it. And that will be part of the overall enterprise value.

items.statement: Target INR 1,500/t EBITDA at Penna (from INR 600-700/t currently) via INR 550/t margin expansion program + INR 300-400/t logistics/debottlenecking
items.quote: And that's why it will go to INR1500. And also mind you, current price line in South is one of the lowest. So, over a long period, I don't think the prices will be there.

items.statement: South demand growth expected from new AP regime; new capacity creation slowed; M&A better than greenfield for industry
items.quote: Mind you, there will be a substantial growth in large parts of the country, especially with the new regime in place in AP. I believe there should be a lot of development work.

items.statement: Penna plants well-maintained with captive power, WHR, railway sidings (except Talaricheruvu); experienced team to integrate with Ambuja/ACC operations
items.quote: All plants have their own railway siding, very good limestone reserves, very good equipment, very well maintain ed plant a nd all the bulk terminals are very efficient, fully automated both packing machines.

items.statement: Volume growth up 15-17% quarter-on-quarter despite Red Sea crisis
items.quote: our overall volume growth from quarter to quarter has gone up by close to more than 15%, around 17%

items.statement: Launched FreightJar Version 2.0 with global access and better features
items.quote: we were able to finalize the Version 2 of our logistics online platform Freight Jar which will definitely give us better access to more markets and better access to more customers & clients who are dealing in the international business

items.statement: Imports business growing in electronics, raw materials, PTA and polyester
items.quote: development of our imports department, which we've been trying for the last few years, but I take pride in saying that, yes that department is shaping up well so now our business on imports is also growing where we are working very close in the electronic goods and raw materials for the electronic markets and also our growing business in the PTA, polyester fabrics and polyester manufacturer as wel

items.statement: Added new steel customers including Jindal Steel contract performing well
items.quote: our contract with Jindal Steel is doing very well. I think along with that we've added few more steel customers

items.statement: Business outlook bullish for current and coming quarters
items.quote: overall the business scenario is looking very bullish, this quarter has started well. I would say that we are, we are doing well in this quarter

items.statement: Red Sea crisis, port congestion and container shortages to persist 2-3 quarters
items.quote: we are expecting that at least for the next 2-3 quarters, this is going to continue

items.statement: Cost-plus model passes freight increases to customers, improving margins
items.quote: since we are in the cost-plus model, you know we will have to pass on this increase to our customer. So, I don't think it will have any negative impact, but definitely it will have a positive impact because any freight increase definitely also increases the overall margins as well

items.statement: FreightJar onboarded 250+ new customers in first year
items.quote: we were able to atleast register close to 250 plus new customers which were onboarded and that was an increase in the business

items.statement: FreightJar revenue model maintains 7-8% margin same as core business
items.quote: The revenue model is purely what we are doing now. Since it is a sales product of Tiger Logistics, we are offering the same services through the online portal. So, the margin remains the same at 7%-8% whatever is there in our business

items.statement: Targeting higher import share to reduce export dependence
items.quote: We don't want to be purely dependent on exports. So that was our aim to get those numbers going, so we are looking at imports also to be a very sustainable vertical for us

items.statement: Shanghai-Chennai 40ft container rate jumped from $800 to $4,500
items.quote: in the month of February'24 and March'24, the 120 feet container from Shanghai to Chennai was around $800 and same container today is at $4,500, 40 feet container

items.statement: Container shortages and blank sailings causing congestion and skipped schedules
items.quote: There is a lot of congestion that is also happening. Skipping also is taking place, blank sailing is also taking place. So that is only adding to the problem

items.statement: Inorganic growth via LCL acquisition pending due to lack of aligned targets
items.quote: the only thing which is lacking is that we were looking at some kind of inorganic growth in terms of acquiring LCL company, which has not happened because you know we were not able to get the company which is aligned to our idea of growth

items.statement: Government projects business winning contracts (HPCL, BHEL)
items.quote: Development of the government projects business, it's doing well for us. We've got some good contracts this quarter as well

items.statement: China export bans shifting business to India, benefiting logistics
items.quote: whatever is getting banned, it's getting transferred either to India or to Vietnam or to other countries. So definitely the Indian international business is going to grow and that benefit will definitely come on to us

items.statement: Red Sea crisis continues with no vessels transiting despite less media coverage
items.quote: No, it is just that it's not in the news, but no containers are going from there, no vessels are going from there

items.statement: Order book exceeds INR 40 crores
items.quote: With a diverse product portfolio of over 25 SKUs and a robust order book of exceeding INR 40 crores, we serve B2B customers across defense, marine, offshore, oil and gas and other industries.

items.statement: Targets 25-30% year-on-year sustainable revenue growth
items.quote: So I think we will be able to achieve a very sustainable growth of 25%, 30% year-on-year. So that is also our target to be sustainable.

items.statement: Foundry backward integration may add 3% to PAT margin over time
items.quote: It is possible that the foundry will add to somewhere shares increase the margin, I think, by 3%. It is possible. Yes.

items.statement: Present CapEx around INR 15 crores as of May 2024; FY25 CapEx still in planning
items.quote: Present we have around 15 CR CapEx. So we are planning yeah. Yeah. We are planning to have some more machineries, technological machine s and equipment in future so we can enhance our productivity also with the new technologies we will have increase in the ROCE

items.statement: Foundry integration expected to increase throughput by 30-40%
items.quote: I can say if you just put it in numbers literally, it will be 30%, 40% increase.

items.statement: Foundry integration in process, expected to be ready in a couple of months
items.quote: It is in process. The integration is in process , we expect that another couple of months will go down the line. But that is identified, and we are doing it. Yes.

items.statement: Domestic defense and marine demand driving 100% capacity utilization, exports deprioritized
items.quote: So our capacity utilization was almost 100% just for domestic. So, that is the reason why we were running. We strategically did not go for export because the demand from domestic was very high.

items.statement: Defense and marine to contribute 50-60% of revenue; niche in nonferrous valves with high quality standards
items.quote: 50-60% revenues will come only from defense. If we focus and continue our product for a expansion, continue to give more value-added services to our clients, we will be having a very stable and sustainable and good revenue with good margin from defense and marine industry.

items.statement: JV with Nibe Meson Naval Limited for value-added piping fabrication services; full management in place by September, revenue expected in H2
items.quote: The JV, the management will be in place from September. But at the same time, we are liaisoning with the concerned authorities for upcoming projects, putting what value added services we can provide, all these things are in discussions. But the full-scale management will be in place from September onwards, 1st September onwards. So we think that second half, we can see some revenues coming from th

items.statement: License agreement with Georg Schunemann GmbH for automatic cleaning filter technology; 80% Make in India, 20% parts from Germany
items.quote: Make in India. And some parts, say, around 20% parts will come from Germany, 80% of it will be made in India.

items.quote: That plant is also not operating at optimum capacity around 30%, 40% only, they have some technical and social issues, but hopefully from next year 24-25, it should improve the performance with all whatever step they are taking for plant improvement.

items.statement: Industrial plants (caprolactam, melamine) running above 100% capacity
items.quote: All plants are working on more than 100% capacity.

items.statement: Subsidy policy erratic; retrospective reductions create unpredictability in fertilizer EBITDA
items.quote: Because whatever I produce even now, say in August, if I sell it in October, it will fetch reduced subsidy. So when we'll be able to know, farmer will take the fertilizer from retail point, it is very, very difficult to predict.

items.statement: Nano urea and nano DAP/NPK at lab scale; test marketing in FY24, commercialization later
items.quote: In case of your question for nano-urea, it's still in the lab scale at our end for manufacturing, but we are looking out for the tie-ups also. And other nano fertilizers like, DAP or NPK, it's still in the lab scale status only.

items.statement: Baroda unit fully backward integrated; Sikka unit partially integrated; both units ~10 lakh tons each
items.quote: In Baroda we are fully backward integrated. In Sikar we are in the process of getting backward integrated to some extent not fully. It will be a phase manner but yes in Baroda we are 100% backward integrated.

items.statement: Dividend consistency to be maintained in line with earnings
items.quote: Only thing I can say is that there will be consistency in dividend in line with the earnings. So if there are earnings, I think management will not hold the dividend belonging to shareholders.

items.statement: Agriculture season favorable with widespread rainfall and good reservoir levels supporting volume growth
items.quote: Season is still good because now there's a widespread rainfall as well as reservoir levels are good. And so that will occur well for rubby season also and based on that only, we see rise in the volume.

items.statement: India cheapest fertilizer market globally; imports at $100-200/t premium to domestic prices
items.quote: Price parity, if you see the prices of trade across various countries of fertilizers, India is the cheapest country, we are taking on the cheapest prices. If you go to Bangladesh also, they are still $100 more. I'm giving an average figure to you. If you go to Brazil, it is $200 more per ton on average basis.

items.statement: Shutdown maintenance cost INR25-30 crore in Q1; planned turnaround every 4 years
items.quote: So it comes to around, say, INR25 crores, INR30 crores. It depends, if you want to change major equipment and it can be more also.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 30% year-on-year
items.quote: We expect to grow our revenue by 30% in FY25.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin improvement guidance of 1.5 percentage points
items.quote: Due to an increase in occupancy and operating leverage on costs, we should be able to improve our EBITDA margins by approximately 1.5% for FY25 versus FY24.

items.statement: FY25 seat addition target of ~40,000 new seats reaching ~135,000 total seats
items.quote: We plan to add around ~40,000 new seats in FY25 reaching a total of ~135,000 seats by end of FY25.

items.statement: FY25 capex expected in similar range to FY24's INR142 crores
items.quote: Our capex spends excluding the right of use assets for FY24 stood at INR142 crores while for FY25 we expect capex spends in a very similar range.

items.statement: 181 centers with 1,10,540 seats as of March 2024, 21 centers under fit-out

items.quote: In terms of new openings during the year, 43 new centers were launched with 79% centers under managed aggregation model and 27,490 new seats were added with 79% seats in managed aggregation model.

items.statement: 15,500 seats under fit-out and 16,522 seats with signed LOI as of March 2024
items.quote: As of March 24, we already have approximately 15,500 seats in the fit outs and for approximately 16,500 seats we have signed LOI in place.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin at 31%, Q4 FY24 at 31.5%, IND-AS 116 adjusted EBITDA at 10.4%
items.quote: The EBITDA stood at INR271 crores which is a growth of 54% on a year-on-year basis. The margins stood at 31% for FY24 and at 31.5% for Q4 FY24.

items.statement: IND-AS 116 adjusted EBITDA improved to 10.4% in FY24 from 4.3% in FY23
items.quote: On IND-AS 116 adjusted basis the EBITDA has improved to 10.4% in FY24 against a 4.3% in FY23 on the back of strong revenue growth and operating efficiencies.

items.statement: Flexible workspace penetration expected to rise from 12.5% to 16% by 2026, seat take-up CAGR ~42%
items.quote: The penetration level of flexible work space sector in the office space non-SEZ segment has seen a steep jump from 9% in 2020 to 12.5% in December 2023. This is expected to rise to 16% on the expanded base in 2026.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 73% co-working space & allied services, 24% construction & fit-out projects
items.quote: In FY24, 73% of the revenues came from the co-working space on rent and allied services, 24% from construction and fit-out projects and the balance from others.

items.statement: Top 5 clients contribute 13.8% of space revenue, largest client 4.9%, 68% seats from large corporates/MNCs
items.quote: Our revenue base is extremely diversified. Top five clients contributed 13.8% to space revenues while the largest client stood at 4.9% share. Based on number of occupied seats, ~68% of client base belongs to large corporates or multinational companies.

items.statement: Cohort >100 seats increased from 50% in FY21 to 58% in FY24
items.quote: Our cohort of over 100 seats has been steadily increasing and now it stands to 58% (was erroneously mentioned as 48% on earnings call) in FY24, from 50% in FY21 to 58% in FY24 demonstrating the growing confidence of our clients with larger cohorts in us

items.statement: Pricing ranges INR6,000-18,000 per seat per month, driven by center EBITDA margin and payback period
items.quote: Our pricing of the product on a per se at basis ranges from about INR6,000 to INR18,000 per seat per month. We expect that we will follow a similar kind of rule and the financial metrics to determine the pricing.

items.statement: Existing center escalations 4-6% for large cohorts, 5-8% for smaller cohorts
items.quote: Generally, for a larger cohort these escalations range from about 4% to 6%. And for a smaller cohort it ranges from about 5% to 8%.

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR228 crores, OCF/EBITDA 84% in FY24
items.quote: Operating cash flows for FY24 stood at INR228 crores and accordingly OCF to EBITDA stood at 84% which indicates a very healthy cash conversion ratio.

items.statement: Gross debt INR32 crores, net debt negative INR25 crores, gross debt/equity 0.13
items.quote: Our debt at consolidated level stood at INR32 crores. Gross debt to equity is at 0.13. At the net level, we are a debt-free company and net debt to equity ratio is at minus 0.1.

items.statement: IPO of INR599 crores (INR129 crores fresh issue) for capex, working capital, general corporate purposes
items.quote: We recently concluded our IPO of INR 599 crores through a combination of fresh issue of INR129 crores and an offer for sale of INR 471 crores by selling shareholders. We propose to utilize the net proceeds from fresh issue towards funding capital expenditure towards establishment of new centers, funding our working capital requirements and general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Weighted average total tenure ~33 months, lock-in tenure ~24 months, both steadily increasing
items.quote: Currently, total weighted average tenure of the portfolio is approximately 33 months while the total weighted average lock-in tenure is at 24 months. These two metrics are steadily increasing.

items.statement: ROCE 43% for FY24, annualized 53% for Q4 FY24
items.quote: Our ROCE stood at 43% for FY 24 and on an annualized basis it is at 53% for Q4 FY24.

items.statement: Center capex ~INR1,700-1,800 per sq ft, similar for MA and SL models with 5-8% site variability
items.quote: We end up spending about INR1,700-INR1,800 per square feet on the center capex. So, irrespective of that center being under managed aggregation or straight lease model, the difference generally in a capex varies from a bit site-to-site depending on the site condition.

items.statement: In-house design, project management, procurement; 150+ in-house project managers/designers, execution via partner network
items.quote: We built the in-house design and project management team and a very strong procurement team. So, all of the design, majority of the project management and all of the procurement happens in-house. Then we leverage our extended partners who basically do the execution at site.

items.quote: We expect revenues from export business to increase quite significantly as a percentage of total revenues over the years from the current contribution of low double-digits to 30% by FY '27.

items.quote: During 2025, we expect both entities to generate INR600 crores to INR650 crores of revenue and a PAT of INR15 crores to INR17 crores.

items.statement: Aiming for INR6,000 crores revenue, 3-4% PAT margin and 25% ROCE long-term
items.quote: We are looking to achieve INR6,000 crores revenue, 3% to 4% PAT margin and of 25% ROCE.

items.statement: Existing factory with minimal capex can support over INR5,000 crores revenue
items.quote: Our existing factory alone with minimal investment in capital expenditure can let us grow more than INR5,000 crores in revenues.

items.statement: Sky Gold capacity 750 kg/month, currently using 350-375 kg/month; acquired entities 50 kg/month, can go to 200-300 kg/month
items.quote: Skygold we have a capacity of 750 kg per month. Last year we used 270 kg per month. This year we have started using it 350 kg to 400 kg per month.

items.statement: Target 50% capacity utilization at new facility on annualized basis in FY25
items.quote: Looking ahead to financial year '25, our roadmap would be to increase capacity utilization at our new facility to 50% on an annualized basis.

items.quote: On the balance sheet side, our inventory days increased due to the corporate orders which were received close to the end of the quarter.

items.quote: The gross margin was at 7.2%. The quarterly volatility in gross margins is due to product mix change. Structurally, we would like to reach 7% to 8% gross margins through product mix and exports.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to be maintained at 5-5.5% long term

items.quote: EBITDA is around 4-4.4% in the last year. So we will improve that. And PAT is about 2% approx.

items.quote: Over the next couple of quarters, we would be moving to 80-90% gold metal loan at 3%. With a gold metal loan, there would be no hedging costs as well.

items.quote: As a result of conversation from working capital loan to GML and liquidation of shares, our interest costs would more than drop by half to less than 0.5% of the sales.

items.statement: Target to lower capital cycle to 45 days over next two years, inventory days normalized below 35 days
items.quote: Over the next two years, we would like to lower the capital cycle to 45 days. Even the receivable days would reduce with more cash and carry business.
